# rgflux

> Rare event kinetics over rgsaddle and rgmin.

The Rust API separates rate estimators and trajectory sampling from
potential energy surfaces and molecular dynamics engines.

## Complete documentation

## rgflux

       </div>
     </div>

`rgflux` separates rare-event kinetics from specific force fields and molecular dynamics codes. Every sampler drives the `DynamicsEngine` trait, while recorded trajectory estimators such as `kappa::bennett_chandler` stay engine-free.

   :maxdepth: 1
   :caption: Guides

## Getting started

## Install

Add `rgflux` from crates.io (alongside `ndarray` and `rgsaddle` when defining custom potential surfaces) cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025`:

```console
$ cargo add rgflux
```

Enable optional `rgpot`, `rgpot-session`, and `lammpc` features as needed:

```console
$ cargo add rgflux --features rgpot
$ cargo add rgflux --features rgpot-session
$ cargo add rgflux --features lammpc
```

The `lammpc` feature links `liblammpc` from `LAMMPC_LIB_DIR`, from `pkg-config` when available, or from `LAMMPC_DIR` (install prefix with `lib/` or `lib64/` and `include/`) when `pkg-config` is not configured. Include both `liblammpc` and its LAMMPS runtime on the loader path. Its build also needs the `capnp` command-line tool on `PATH`. `--all-features` therefore requires those libraries; builds with no features, or with `rgpot` or `rgpot-session`, do not.

## 1. Engine-free Bennett-Chandler recrossing

`kappa::bennett_chandler::estimate_bennett_chandler` estimates the time-dependent transmission coefficient \(\kappa(t)\) and its stationary plateau mean with a block-averaged standard error from `stats` cite:`bennettMolecularDynamics1977,chandlerStatisticalMechanics1978,flegalMcmcThirdSignificantFigure2008` directly from recorded dividing-surface velocity and side histories:

```rust
use rgflux::kappa::bennett_chandler::{
    BennettChandlerConfig, ReactiveTrajectory, Side, estimate_bennett_chandler,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let trajectories = vec![
        ReactiveTrajectory::new(1.2, vec![Side::Product; 16])?,
        ReactiveTrajectory::new(-0.9, vec![Side::Reactant; 16])?,
        ReactiveTrajectory::new(0.8, vec![Side::Product; 16])?,
    ];
    let estimate = estimate_bennett_chandler(&trajectories, &BennettChandlerConfig::default())?;
    assert_eq!(estimate.plateau, 1.0);
    assert_eq!(estimate.standard_error, 0.0);
    assert!(estimate.stationarity.is_stationary);
    Ok(())
}
```

## 2. Climb the free energy of a dividing hyperplane (OH-TST)

Optimal hyperplanar transition state theory takes the dividing surface to be a hyperplane and moves it until its free energy is a maximum cite:`johannessonOptimizationHyperplanar2001`. A converged dimer from `rgsaddle` seeds the plane, and `ohtst::PlaneOptimizer` climbs the plane free energy with short constrained Langevin samples. The surface is the skewed double well \(V = (x^2 - 1)^2 + \tfrac12 k(x)(y - x)^2\) with \(k(x) = 4(1 + 0.8 \tanh 2x)\), already in mass-weighted coordinates.

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1, array};
use rgflux::ohtst::{Hyperplane, LangevinConfig, PlaneOptimizer, PlaneOptimizerConfig};
use rgsaddle::{MinModeConfig, MinModeSession, MinModeStatus, PointSurface, SaddleError};

struct SkewedWell;

impl PointSurface for SkewedWell {
    fn eval(&self, q: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), SaddleError> {
        let (x, y) = (q[0], q[1]);
        let (well, tanh, valley) = (x * x - 1.0, (2.0 * x).tanh(), y - x);
        let k = 4.0 * (1.0 + 0.8 * tanh);
        let energy = well * well + 0.5 * k * valley * valley;
        let gx = 4.0 * x * well + 3.2 * (1.0 - tanh * tanh) * valley * valley - k * valley;
        Ok((energy, array![gx, k * valley]))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let search = MinModeConfig::default().with_force_tol(1e-8);
    let mut dimer = MinModeSession::new(search, array![0.1, -0.05], array![1.0, 0.3])?;
    assert_eq!(dimer.run(&SkewedWell, 2000)?.status, MinModeStatus::Converged);
    let seed = Hyperplane::from_min_mode(&dimer)?.oriented_toward(array![1.0, 1.0].view());

    let sampler = LangevinConfig::default()
        .with_thermal(0.1)
        .with_time_step(0.1)
        .with_burn_in(200)
        .with_records(400)
        .with_seed(9);
    let config = PlaneOptimizerConfig::default()
        .with_sampler(sampler)
        .with_max_records(400)
        .with_max_iterations(10);
    let optimum = PlaneOptimizer::new(&seed, config)?.run(&SkewedWell)?;

    let normal = optimum.plane.normal();
    assert!((normal.dot(&normal) - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12);
    assert!(normal[0] > 0.0 && normal[1] > 0.0);
    Ok(())
}
```

## How-to guides

## Sample holonomic hyperplane mean forces and configurations

Construct a `HyperplaneConstraint` from a direction vector and scalar offset \(c\), configure `HyperplaneConfig`, and call `hyperplane::sample_hyperplane` over any `DynamicsEngine` cite:`sprikFreeEnergyConstrained1998,leimkuhlerGeodesicIntegration2016`. `sample_hyperplane` installs the constraint, runs BAOAB + RATTLE equilibration and production steps, estimates \(\langle \lambda \rangle = dA/dc\) with a block-averaged standard error, retains dividing-surface configurations every `retention_stride` steps, and restores the engine's initial positions, velocities, periodic cell, thermostat, and constraint before returning:

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, HyperplaneConstraint, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::hyperplane::{HyperplaneConfig, sample_hyperplane};

struct DoubleWell2D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for DoubleWell2D {
    fn eval(&self, r: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let (x, y) = (r[0], r[1]);
        let well = x * x - 1.0;
        Ok((
            0.25 * well * well + 0.5 * y * y,
            Array1::from_vec(vec![x * well, y]),
        ))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        DoubleWell2D,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 1.0]))
            .with_thermostat(
                ThermostatConfig::default()
                    .with_gamma(1.0)
                    .with_temperature(0.2),
            )
            .with_seed(11),
    )?;
    engine.set_positions(Array1::from_vec(vec![-0.3, 0.0]).view())?;

    let plane =
        HyperplaneConstraint::from_direction(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 0.0]).view(), -0.3)?;
    let cfg = HyperplaneConfig::default()
        .with_burn_in_steps(100)
        .with_sample_steps(400)
        .with_retention_stride(20)
        .with_time_step(0.01)
        .with_seed(11);

    let sample = sample_hyperplane(&mut engine, &plane, &cfg)?;
    assert!(sample.mean_force.is_finite());
    assert!(sample.standard_error >= 0.0);
    assert_eq!(sample.configurations.dim(), (20, 2));
    assert!(engine.constraint().is_none());
    Ok(())
}
```

## Diagnose correlated samples with batch means, effective sample size, and Geweke windows

Use `stats::batch_means` for the mean and its correlation-aware standard
error, `stats::effective_sample_size` for the Geyer initial monotone sequence
estimate, and `stats::check_stationarity` before accepting an equilibrium or
plateau window
cite:`goswamiBayesianHierarchical2025,flyvbjergErrorEstimates1989,geyerPracticalMcmc1992,gewekeEvaluatingAccuracy1992,flegalMcmcThirdSignificantFigure2008`.

For \(a\) non-overlapping batches of width \(b\), batch means \(Y_j\), and
\(n = ab\) retained observations, the asymptotic variance and standard error
are

\[
 \widehat{\sigma}_{\mathrm{BM}}^2 =
 \frac{b}{a - 1}\sum_{j=1}^{a}(Y_j-\bar{Y})^2,\qquad
 \operatorname{SE}(\bar{X}) =
 \sqrt{\widehat{\sigma}_{\mathrm{BM}}^2/n}.
\]

Geyer's paired initial positive and monotone autocovariance sequence gives the
statistical inefficiency \(g = 2\tau_{\mathrm{int}}\) and
\(n_{\mathrm{eff}} = n/g\). The Geweke diagnostic compares leading and
trailing windows with

\[
 \lvert z\rvert =
 \frac{|\bar{X}_{\mathrm{first}}-\bar{X}_{\mathrm{last}}|}
 {\sqrt{\operatorname{SE}_{\mathrm{first}}^2+
        \operatorname{SE}_{\mathrm{last}}^2}}.
\]

```rust
use rgflux::stats::{
    StatsConfig, batch_means, check_stationarity, effective_sample_size,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let samples: Vec<f64> = (0..256)
        .map(|i| {
            let phase = (i % 16) as f64;
            (phase * std::f64::consts::TAU / 16.0).sin()
        })
        .collect();
    let config = StatsConfig::default()
        .with_min_batches(8)
        .with_stationarity_first_fraction(0.25)
        .with_stationarity_last_fraction(0.50)
        .with_max_z_score(3.0);

    let estimate = batch_means(&samples, &config)?;
    let n_eff = effective_sample_size(&samples)?;
    let stationarity = check_stationarity(&samples, &config)?;

    assert!(estimate.standard_error >= 0.0);
    assert_eq!(estimate.n_eff, n_eff);
    assert!(n_eff >= 1.0 && n_eff <= samples.len() as f64);
    assert!(stationarity.is_stationary);
    Ok(())
}
```

## Assemble a rate-network edge and kMC configuration

A directed rate network stores non-negative first-order rates \(k_{ij}\).
Its continuous-time master equation is

\[
 \frac{dp_i}{dt} =
 \sum_{j\ne i} p_j k_{ji} -
 p_i\sum_{j\ne i}k_{ij}.
\]
For a BKL or Gillespie residence-time step in state \(i\), define
\(K_i = \sum_j k_{ij}\), select event \(j\) with probability
\(k_{ij}/K_i\), and draw
\(\Delta t = -\ln u/K_i\) for \(u\) uniform on \((0,1)\)
cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,goswamiConcurrencyAkmc2025,bortzNewAlgorithmMonteCarlo1975,gillespieGeneralMethod1976,henkelmanLongTimeScale2001`.

`RateEdge::new` validates one directed edge. `NetworkConfig` records thermal
and detailed-balance policy, while `RateTableConfig` records trajectory
limits. `build_rate_table` is deliberately a typed migration boundary in this
release and returns `FluxError::Unimplemented` rather than silently producing
an incomplete table.

```rust
use rgflux::FluxError;
use rgflux::network::{
    NetworkConfig, RateEdge, RateTableConfig, build_rate_table,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let edges = vec![
        RateEdge::new(0, 1, 2.0)?,
        RateEdge::new(1, 0, 0.5)?,
    ];
    let network = NetworkConfig::default()
        .with_temperature(500.0)
        .with_boltzmann(1.0)
        .with_enforce_detailed_balance(true)
        .with_min_rate(1.0e-12);
    let trajectory = RateTableConfig::default()
        .with_max_steps(10_000)
        .with_seed(7);

    assert_eq!(trajectory.max_steps, 10_000);
    assert!(matches!(
        build_rate_table(2, &edges, &network),
        Err(FluxError::Unimplemented(_))
    ));
    Ok(())
}
```

## Compute a transition rate with direct Forward Flux Sampling (FFS)

Initialize the engine inside reactant basin \(A\) (\(\lambda(\mathbf{x}_0) \le \lambda_0\)) with positive Langevin friction \(\gamma > 0\), specify strictly increasing interfaces \(\lambda_0 < \lambda_1 < \dots < \lambda_n\) in `FfsConfig`, and pass an order-parameter closure \(\lambda(\mathbf{x})\) to `ffs::forward_flux_rate` cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,allenSamplingRareSwitching2005,allenSimulatingRareEvents2006,allenForwardFluxEfficiency2006,allenForwardFluxReview2009`:

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::ffs::{FfsConfig, forward_flux_rate};

struct QuarticDoubleWell1D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for QuarticDoubleWell1D {
    fn eval(&self, x: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let dx = x[0] * x[0] - 1.0;
        Ok((dx * dx, Array1::from_vec(vec![4.0 * x[0] * dx])))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let cfg = NativeConfig::default()
        .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0]))
        .with_thermostat(
            ThermostatConfig::default()
                .with_gamma(2.0)
                .with_temperature(0.9),
        )
        .with_seed(11);
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(QuarticDoubleWell1D, cfg)?;
    engine.set_positions(Array1::from_vec(vec![-1.0]).view())?;
    engine.shoot_velocities(11)?;

    let ffs_cfg = FfsConfig::default()
        .with_interfaces(vec![-0.8, -0.4, -0.1, 0.2])
        .with_points_per_interface(16)
        .with_trials_per_interface(64)
        .with_max_trial_steps(3_000)
        .with_max_flux_steps(400_000)
        .with_burn_in_steps(50)
        .with_time_step(0.01)
        .with_seed(11);

    let est = forward_flux_rate(&mut engine, |x| x[0], &ffs_cfg)?;
    assert!(est.initial_flux > 0.0);
    assert_eq!(est.interface_probabilities.len(), 3);
    assert!(est.rate > 0.0 && est.standard_error > 0.0);
    assert_eq!(engine.positions()[0], -1.0);
    Ok(())
}
```

## Compute a free-energy profile, barrier and rate along a reaction path (PAFI workflow)

Projected Average Force Integration (PAFI) cite:`goswamiEnhancedClimbingImage2026,goswamiReproducibleOrchestration2026,swinburneUnsupervisedCalculation2018` takes the images of a converged minimum-energy path, for example from a nudged elastic band, and returns the free-energy profile \(F(s)\), the barrier \(\Delta F\), the dividing plane, and the normalized rate \(k\) through `pafi::pafi_profile`. The method is described under /Projected Average Force Integration/ in the explanation page and the defaults in the reference page.

The example runs a straight path from the minimum \(x = -1\) to the saddle \(x = 0\) of the widening double well \(V(x, y) = (1 - x^2)^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}(1.5 + 0.5x)y^2\) at \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T = 0.2\), where the exact barrier is \(\Delta F = 1 + \tfrac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T \ln 1.5\). It uses 33 planes. The free-energy profile is the cubic Hermite integral of the plane means, so the trapezoid bias of about \(0.0156\,(8/(\text{planes} - 1))^2\) (0.025 with the default 9 planes, 0.0016 with 33) is the scale of the zero-temperature guard and is not left in \(\Delta F\). The run checks the barrier within five standard errors.

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, Array2, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::ThermostatConfig;
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::pafi::{PafiConfig, pafi_profile};
use rgflux::stats::StatsConfig;

struct WideningWell2D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for WideningWell2D {
    fn eval(&self, r: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let (x, y) = (r[0], r[1]);
        let well = 1.0 - x * x;
        let k = 1.5 + 0.5 * x;
        Ok((
            well * well + 0.5 * k * y * y,
            Array1::from_vec(vec![-4.0 * x * well + 0.25 * y * y, k * y]),
        ))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let temperature = 0.2;
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        WideningWell2D,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 1.0]))
            .with_thermostat(
                ThermostatConfig::default()
                    .with_gamma(1.5)
                    .with_temperature(temperature),
            )
            .with_seed(19),
    )?;

    // PAFI samples at `config.planes` planes along a spline through these
    // images. Two images would do for a straight path; a curved path needs
    // the images of the converged band.
    let config = PafiConfig::default()
        .with_planes(33)
        .with_burn_in_steps(500)
        .with_sample_steps(8_000)
        .with_stats(StatsConfig::default().with_min_batches(4))
        .with_seed(19);
    let images = 5;
    let mut path = Array2::<f64>::zeros((images, 2));
    for k in 0..images {
        path[[k, 0]] = -1.0 + (k as f64) / ((images - 1) as f64);
    }

    let profile = pafi_profile(&mut engine, path.view(), &config)?;
    assert_eq!(profile.arc_lengths.len(), config.planes);
    assert_eq!(profile.free_energy[0], 0.0);
    assert_eq!(profile.dividing_index, config.planes - 1);

    let analytic = 1.0 + 0.5 * temperature * 1.5_f64.ln();
    assert!(profile.barrier_error > 0.0);
    assert!((profile.barrier - analytic).abs() < 5.0 * profile.barrier_error);
    assert!(
        profile.normalized_rate.is_some_and(|rate| rate > 0.0)
            && profile
                .normalized_rate_error
                .is_some_and(|error| error > 0.0)
    );
    Ok(())
}
```

Points to adapt for a real path:

- *Images*: `path_images` has one row per image and one column per degree of freedom, in the units and ordering of the engine. The planes are placed by the spline, not at the images, so the number of images and `planes` are independent.
- *Planes and tolerance*: The zero-temperature check compares \(\lvert I_T - \Delta E_0\rvert / \max(E_{\mathrm{unit}}, \lvert\Delta E_0\rvert)\) with a dimensionless tolerance. Here \(I_T\) is the trapezoid integral of \(dV/ds\), \(\Delta E_0\) is the endpoint energy change and \(E_{\mathrm{unit}}\) is one energy unit of the engine. `zero_temperature_tol` is `Option<f64>`. `None`, the default, uses \(2 (\pi^2 / 12) / (\text{planes} - 1)^2\), about 2.6% at 9 planes, and scales when `planes` changes. `with_zero_temperature_tol` sets a value used at every plane count, including a value equal to the 9-plane tolerance. A sharper path can require a larger explicit tolerance. A failing check returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` before any sampling.
- *Statistical error*: Set `with_target_error(0.01)` and `with_max_rounds(8)` to repeat sampling in rounds of `sample_steps` until `barrier_error` reaches the target. Reaching `max_rounds` first is not an error, so compare `barrier_error` with the target yourself.
- *Reproducibility*: The seed of plane \(k\) in round \(r\) is `seed + 4099 * k + 1000003 * r`, so a fixed `with_seed` gives the same profile for a deterministic engine.
- *Thermostat*: The engine needs a supported canonical thermostat. White noise requires \(\gamma > 0\); its \(\gamma = 0\) NVE mode returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig`. A supported colored-noise thermostat can remain canonical at \(\gamma = 0\). Any canonical setting targets the same profile, so choose the thermostat parameters for the standard error and the burn-in.
- *Engine*: `pafi_profile_dyn` accepts `&mut dyn DynamicsEngine`. The engine is restored on return, with the stochastic stream the only exception.

## Scan the displacement between two atom groups

`pafi::group_displacement_scan` fixes \(s = \mathbf{n}\cdot(\mathbf{R}_B-\mathbf{R}_A)\) on each window and lets the other degrees of freedom relax. Indices are 0-based atom indices. Pass `&[]` for `rigid_groups` when no rigid constraint is installed. The sampling arguments are a `HyperplaneConfig`. The reported mean force is the hyperplane multiplier divided by the Euclidean norm of \(\nabla s\), and `free_energy` is its cubic Hermite integral cite:`sprikFreeEnergyConstrained1998,swinburneUnsupervisedCalculation2018`.

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::hyperplane::HyperplaneConfig;
use rgflux::pafi::group_displacement_scan;

struct PairSpring;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for PairSpring {
    fn eval(&self, x: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let s = x[3] - x[0];
        let mut gradient = Array1::zeros(6);
        gradient[0] = -s;
        gradient[3] = s;
        Ok((0.5 * s * s, gradient))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        PairSpring,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_elem(6, 1.0))
            .with_thermostat(ThermostatConfig::default().with_gamma(1.0).with_temperature(0.0)),
    )?;
    engine.set_positions(Array1::from_vec(vec![0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0]).view())?;
    let config = HyperplaneConfig::default()
        .with_burn_in_steps(0)
        .with_sample_steps(2)
        .with_time_step(0.05);
    let profile = group_displacement_scan(
        &mut engine,
        &[0],
        &[1],
        Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 0.0, 0.0]).view(),
        &[0.0, 0.5],
        &[],
        &config,
    )?;
    assert!((profile.mean_forces[1] - 0.5).abs() < 1.0e-8);
    assert!(engine.constraint().is_none());
    Ok(())
}
```

## Shoot Bennett-Chandler reactive-flux trajectories and compare with Kramers

Combine `hyperplane::sample_hyperplane` (to harvest thermalized configurations on the dividing surface \(x = 0\)) with `kappa::bennett_chandler::shoot_bennett_chandler` and compare the resulting plateau transmission coefficient against `kappa::kramers_transmission_coefficient` cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,bennettMolecularDynamics1977,chandlerStatisticalMechanics1978,kramersBrownianMotion1940`:

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{HyperplaneConstraint, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::hyperplane::{HyperplaneConfig, sample_hyperplane};
use rgflux::kappa::bennett_chandler::{
    KappaConfig, ShootingConfig, shoot_bennett_chandler,
};
use rgflux::kappa::kramers_transmission_coefficient;

struct SeparableDoubleWell2D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for SeparableDoubleWell2D {
    fn eval(&self, r: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let (x, y) = (r[0], r[1]);
        let dx = x * x - 1.0;
        Ok((dx * dx + y * y, Array1::from_vec(vec![4.0 * x * dx, 2.0 * y])))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let gamma = 6.0;
    let omega_b = 2.0;
    let kramers = kramers_transmission_coefficient(gamma, omega_b)?;

    let dividing_surface =
        HyperplaneConstraint::new(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 0.0]), 0.0)?;
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        SeparableDoubleWell2D,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 1.0]))
            .with_thermostat(
                ThermostatConfig::default()
                    .with_gamma(gamma)
                    .with_temperature(0.08),
            )
            .with_seed(42),
    )?;

    let surface_sample = sample_hyperplane(
        &mut engine,
        &dividing_surface,
        &HyperplaneConfig::default()
            .with_burn_in_steps(100)
            .with_sample_steps(400)
            .with_retention_stride(10)
            .with_time_step(0.02)
            .with_seed(42),
    )?;

    let shoot_cfg = ShootingConfig::default()
        .with_steps(120)
        .with_time_step(0.05)
        .with_antithetic(true)
        .with_kappa(
            KappaConfig::default()
                .with_commit_checkpoints(64)
                .with_commitment_distance(0.25),
        )
        .with_seed(99);
    let bc = shoot_bennett_chandler(
        &mut engine,
        &dividing_surface,
        surface_sample.configurations.view(),
        &shoot_cfg,
    )?;

    assert!(bc.plateau > 0.0 && bc.standard_error > 0.0);
    assert!(kramers > 0.3 && kramers < 0.31);
    Ok(())
}
```

The default integrates every half to `steps`. This example opts into early commitment only after specifying both parts of the criterion: `commit_checkpoints = 64` requires 64 consecutive steps (\(64 \times 0.05 = 3.2 > 1 / \lambda_+ \approx 1.65\)), while `commitment_distance = 0.25` requires every counted point to lie at least 0.25 length units from the dividing surface on the same side. Choose the distance inside a physically characterized basin and the window beyond its recrossing time. If either condition is uncertain, keep the default fixed-length shooting: even a long, deep excursion can return, and early commitment would hide that return.

## Sample a temperature range with multithermal OPES and reweight frames

Multithermal OPES cite:`invernizziUnifiedApproach2020,invernizziRethinkingMetadynamics2020` biases the potential energy \(U\) so that one run at the thermostat temperature \(T_0\) samples every canonical ensemble between \(T_{\min}\) and \(T_{\max}\). It is the method PLUMED provides as `OPES_EXPANDED` over `ECV_MULTITHERMAL` cite:`tribelloPlumed2014,plumedConsortium2019`, with the same defaults and the same state file. The method and its equations are under /Multithermal OPES/ in the explanation page.

1. Build an `opes::OpesMultithermal` from an `OpesMultithermalConfig` and the engine `ThermostatConfig`, which supplies \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\) and, unless `temperature` is set, \(T_0\). Give the range with `OpesMultithermalConfig::range`, fix the count with `with_temp_steps` or leave it `None` to estimate it from the `observation_steps` unbiased samples, or list the temperatures with `OpesMultithermalConfig::set_all`.
2. Share it with `SharedOpesMultithermal::new`, wrap the unbiased surface in `OpesMultithermalSurface`, and build the engine over that surface.
3. Call `run_opes_multithermal` with an `OpesRunConfig`. Every `frame_stride` steps it stores the unbiased energy \(U_t\), the bias in force \(V_t\), the force factor \(1 + dV/dU\), and the positions.
4. Read `OpesTrajectory::delta_f` for \(\Delta F(T_k)\), and call `OpesTrajectory::weights` with any target temperature in \([T_{\min}, T_{\max}]\). The returned `Vec<f64>` sums to one and has one entry per stored frame, so it can be passed as `&[f64]` to downstream covariance, clustering, or Markov state model code. A target outside the range returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig`.

The frame weights are

\[
w_t(T) = \frac{\exp\bigl(\beta_0 V_t + (\beta_0 - \beta) U_t\bigr)}{\sum_s \exp\bigl(\beta_0 V_s + (\beta_0 - \beta) U_s\bigr)}, \qquad \beta = \frac{1}{k_{\mathrm{B}} T},
\]

the product of the PLUMED `REWEIGHT_BIAS` and `REWEIGHT_TEMP_PRESS` weights. `MultithermalReweighting::average` returns the weighted mean of an observable with a batch-means standard error and the Kish effective sample size \((\sum_t w_t)^2 / \sum_t w_t^2\) cite:`kishSurveySampling1965`. Discard an initial stretch of frames by building `MultithermalReweighting::from_bias` over a slice of the stored energies and biases.

The example samples the 2D double well \(U = (x^2 - 1)^2 + y^2/2\) at \(T_0 = 0.3\) over \([0.3, 1.2]\) and reweights the frames to \(T = 0.8\). There \(\langle y^2 \rangle = k_{\mathrm{B}} T\) exactly, because \(y\) is a harmonic coordinate.

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::opes::{
    OpesMultithermal, OpesMultithermalConfig, OpesMultithermalSurface, OpesRunConfig,
    SharedOpesMultithermal, run_opes_multithermal,
};

struct DoubleWell2D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for DoubleWell2D {
    fn eval(&self, r: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let a = r[0] * r[0] - 1.0;
        Ok((
            a * a + 0.5 * r[1] * r[1],
            Array1::from_vec(vec![4.0 * r[0] * a, r[1]]),
        ))
    }
}

/// Weighted covariance of two per-frame features, as downstream code takes it.
fn weighted_covariance(weights: &[f64], a: &[f64], b: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let mean = |v: &[f64]| weights.iter().zip(v).map(|(w, x)| w * x).sum::<f64>();
    let (ma, mb) = (mean(a), mean(b));
    weights
        .iter()
        .zip(a.iter().zip(b))
        .map(|(w, (x, y))| w * (x - ma) * (y - mb))
        .sum()
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let thermostat = ThermostatConfig::default()
        .with_temperature(0.3)
        .with_gamma(1.0);
    let config = OpesMultithermalConfig::range(0.3, 1.2)
        .with_temp_steps(6)
        .with_pace(50);
    let shared = SharedOpesMultithermal::new(OpesMultithermal::new(config, &thermostat)?);
    let surface = OpesMultithermalSurface::new(DoubleWell2D, shared.clone());
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        surface,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 1.0]))
            .with_thermostat(thermostat)
            .with_seed(11),
    )?;
    engine.set_positions(Array1::from_vec(vec![-1.0, 0.0]).view())?;
    engine.shoot_velocities(11)?;

    let run = OpesRunConfig::default()
        .with_steps(1_000_000)
        .with_time_step(0.01)
        .with_frame_stride(50);
    let trajectory = run_opes_multithermal(&mut engine, &shared, &run)?;
    assert_eq!(trajectory.temperatures().len(), 6);
    assert_eq!(trajectory.delta_f().len(), 6);

    let weights: Vec<f64> = trajectory.weights(0.8)?;
    assert_eq!(weights.len(), trajectory.positions.len());
    let y: Vec<f64> = trajectory.positions.iter().map(|p| p[1]).collect();
    let y_variance = weighted_covariance(&weights, &y, &y);
    assert!((y_variance - 0.8).abs() < 0.05, "<y^2> = {y_variance}");
    assert!(trajectory.weights(1.5).is_err());
    Ok(())
}
```

To continue a run, write `OpesMultithermal::write_state` at the end of one segment and rebuild the bias with `OpesMultithermal::from_state` and the same configuration and thermostat. The file has the layout of the PLUMED `STATE_WFILE`, with the temperature column named `ecv.ene`, so PLUMED can restart from an `rgflux` state and `rgflux` can restart from a PLUMED state.

The restart keeps the update cadence and the thermodynamic reference:

- The bias absorbs a sample only at MD steps that are multiples of `pace`, counted from step 0, so a continuation must keep the absolute step. The state records the last step the bias saw, `from_state` restores it as `OpesMultithermal::last_step`, and `run_opes_multithermal` with the default `OpesRunConfig::start_step` of `None` continues from it. An explicit `start_step` that differs from the restored step returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` before any step is integrated, and so does an update at an earlier step. The configuration at the restored step is not absorbed a second time.
- \(\Delta F\) and `rct` are free energies at \(T_0\) in the energy units of \(U\) and \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T_0\), so they do not carry over to another \(T_0\), \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\), or ladder. The state records \(T_0\), \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\), and the reweighting range \((T_{\min}, T_{\max})\) at full precision, and `from_state` returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` when the configuration and thermostat differ from them beyond a relative \(64\varepsilon\), or when only some of the entries are present.

These entries are comment lines of the form `# rgflux temperature 3e-1`, which PLUMED skips, so the file stays a valid PLUMED state. A state written by PLUMED has none of them, and its six-digit temperature labels can match a ladder built at another \(T_0\) or \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\), so `from_state` returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` for it. Read it with `OpesMultithermal::from_plumed_state`, which takes the \(T_0\) and \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\) the PLUMED run used, for example its `TEMP` and the \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\) of its `UNITS`, and refuses them when they differ from the configuration and thermostat as `from_state` does for recorded entries. `run_opes_multithermal` then requires an explicit `start_step`, since `last_step` is `None`.

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::FluxError;
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::opes::{
    OpesMultithermal, OpesMultithermalConfig, OpesMultithermalSurface, OpesRunConfig,
    SharedOpesMultithermal, run_opes_multithermal,
};

struct DoubleWell;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for DoubleWell {
    fn eval(&self, x: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let a = x[0] * x[0] - 1.0;
        Ok((a * a, Array1::from_vec(vec![4.0 * x[0] * a])))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let thermostat = ThermostatConfig::default().with_temperature(0.3);
    let config = OpesMultithermalConfig::range(0.3, 1.0)
        .with_temp_steps(4)
        .with_pace(10)
        .with_observation_steps(10);
    let shared = SharedOpesMultithermal::new(OpesMultithermal::new(config.clone(), &thermostat)?);
    let surface = OpesMultithermalSurface::new(DoubleWell, shared.clone());
    let native = NativeConfig::default()
        .with_thermostat(thermostat)
        .with_seed(3);
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(surface, native)?;
    engine.set_positions(Array1::from_vec(vec![-1.0]).view())?;
    let run = OpesRunConfig::default().with_steps(1_005).with_time_step(0.01);
    let first = run_opes_multithermal(&mut engine, &shared, &run)?;

    let mut state = Vec::new();
    first.bias.write_state(&mut state, 1_005.0 * 0.01)?;

    // Same configuration and thermostat; `start_step` stays `None`, so the
    // second segment continues at the stored step 1005.
    let restored = OpesMultithermal::from_state(config.clone(), &thermostat, &state[..])?;
    assert_eq!(restored.last_step(), Some(1_005));
    shared.with_bias_mut(|bias| *bias = restored)?;
    let second = run_opes_multithermal(&mut engine, &shared, &run)?;
    assert_eq!(second.steps[0], 1_005);
    assert_eq!(second.last_step, 2_010);

    // Restarting the step count or changing T0 is refused.
    let shifted = run.clone().with_start_step(0);
    assert!(matches!(
        run_opes_multithermal(&mut engine, &shared, &shifted),
        Err(FluxError::InvalidConfig(_))
    ));
    let warmer = thermostat.with_temperature(0.4);
    assert!(matches!(
        OpesMultithermal::from_state(config.clone(), &warmer, &state[..]),
        Err(FluxError::InvalidConfig(_))
    ));

    // A PLUMED state has no rgflux entries; attest T0 and k_B to read it.
    let text = String::from_utf8(state).expect("utf8");
    let plumed: String = text
        .lines()
        .filter(|line| !line.starts_with("# rgflux"))
        .map(|line| format!("{line}\n"))
        .collect();
    assert!(OpesMultithermal::from_state(config.clone(), &thermostat, plumed.as_bytes()).is_err());
    let from_plumed =
        OpesMultithermal::from_plumed_state(config, &thermostat, plumed.as_bytes(), 0.3, 1.0)?;
    assert_eq!(from_plumed.last_step(), None);
    Ok(())
}
```

`tests/opes_plumed_oracle.rs` checks the implementation against PLUMED 2.10.2 built with =--enable-modules=opes=, using the input in `tests/data/opes_plumed/plumed.dat`. Set `RGFLUX_PLUMED` to a `plumed` executable to run it. Without one the test skips and prints why; with =RGFLUX_REQUIRE_PLUMED=1= it fails instead. The `plumed-oracle` CI job builds PLUMED from the release tarball, because the conda-forge package leaves out the `opes` module, and runs the test with skips disallowed. On the replayed double-well frames the two codes agree exactly on every printed \(\Delta F\) and every bias value, to \(4 \times 10^{-16}\) on the bias force, and to \(10^{-14}\) on the reweighted averages, both with fixed, automatic, and listed ladders and across restarts in either direction. PLUMED is needed only for that test.

## Wrap an `rgmin` objective with `EindirSurface`

Any `eindir_core::DifferentiableObjective<f64>` (such as `rgmin::Oracle`) can be adapted into a `ForceSurface` via `engine::EindirSurface` and passed to `NativeEngine`:

```rust
use ndarray::Array1;
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, EindirSurface};

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let oracle = rgmin::Oracle::unbounded(2, |x| {
        let energy = 0.5 * (x[0] * x[0] + 4.0 * x[1] * x[1]);
        let grad = Array1::from_vec(vec![x[0], 4.0 * x[1]]);
        (energy, grad)
    });
    let surface = EindirSurface::new(oracle);
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        surface,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 2.0]))
            .with_seed(7),
    )?;
    engine.shoot_velocities(7)?;
    let report = engine.step(0.01)?;
    assert!(report.potential_energy.is_finite() && report.kinetic_energy.is_finite());
    Ok(())
}
```

## Reference

## Module overview

| Module | Scope | Status |
|---+---+---|
| `engine` | `DynamicsEngine` trait, `ForceSurface`, `EindirSurface`, `HyperplaneConstraint`, `ThermostatConfig`, `SurfaceVelocityPolicy`, `StepReport`, `native` BAOAB/RATTLE backend, optional direct `lammpc` backend, `rgpot` static PES wrapper, and `rgpot-session` MD session skeleton (`openmm`, `nblib`, `lammps`) | Implemented (`native`, `lammpc`, `rgpot`) and `rgpot-session` skeleton |
| `stats` | Batch means, effective sample size `n_eff`, and stationarity diagnostics | Implemented; spline-propagated profile covariance helpers are not yet implemented |
| `kappa::bennett_chandler` | Engine-free reactive-flux estimator and `DynamicsEngine` trajectory shooter | Implemented (including opt-in `KappaConfig::commit_checkpoints` early-commitment stopping) |
| `kappa` | Kramers analytical barrier-recrossing factor and Bennett-Chandler surface shooting | `kramers_transmission_coefficient` and the trajectory shooter are implemented; fixed-length shooting is the default, while opt-in early commitment requires consecutive samples beyond an explicit signed-distance threshold |
| `hyperplane` | Constrained hyperplane sampling (`sample_hyperplane`) and zero-variance control variates | Mean constraint force and configuration retention implemented; the in-plane virial, torque, and control variates are not yet implemented |
| `pafi` | Projected Average Force Integration along reaction paths (`PafiConfig`, `FreeEnergyProfile`, `IntegralEstimate`, `MeanForceIntegral`, `HermiteIntegral`, `SimpsonIntegral`, `pafi_profile`, `pafi_profile_dyn`) and the fixed-cell two-group displacement scan (`group_displacement_scan`) | Implemented: mass-metric spline planes with not-a-knot ends, zero-temperature trapezoid path-force check, burn-in and batch-means sampling per plane, adaptive rounds to a target error, cubic Hermite free-energy profile, global interpolant maximum, doubled-trapezoid reactant partition, projected reactant frequency, barrier, and normalized rate with log-space propagated errors; the two-group scan reuses the hyperplane sampler and the Hermite rule; the engine is restored on return |
| `ohtst` | OH-TST with a fixed hyperplane normal (`optimize_hyperplane`, `optimize_hyperplane_from_minimum`) and reactant relaxation (`relax_reactant`) | Implemented for a fixed normal with `rgsaddle::flux_mass`; normal optimization is not yet implemented |
| `ffs` | Forward Flux Sampling across ordered interfaces (`forward_flux_rate`) | Implemented: flux collection, staged trials, and uncertainty propagation. Exit restores positions, velocities, the periodic cell, the thermostat, and the constraint; the stochastic stream is left where the run put it |
| `opes` | Multithermal OPES expanded-ensemble bias on the potential energy (`OpesMultithermal`, `OpesMultithermalConfig`), biased `ForceSurface` (`OpesMultithermalSurface`), `DynamicsEngine` driver (`run_opes_multithermal`), PLUMED-compatible state files, and per-frame temperature reweighting (`MultithermalReweighting`) | Implemented: PLUMED `OPES_EXPANDED` over `ECV_MULTITHERMAL` defaults, fixed, automatic, and listed ladders, restarts in either direction with PLUMED, and per-frame weights for any temperature in the ladder; multiple walkers, multibaric expansions, and the `CALC_WORK` output are not implemented |
| `network` | Symmetry-resolved rate networks and kinetic Monte Carlo rate tables (`NetworkConfig`, `RateTableConfig`, `RateEdge`, `build_rate_table`) | `RateEdge::new` and configuration types implemented; `build_rate_table` is not yet implemented |
| `cu_reference` | Daw and Chandross Table II copper vacancy mobility record (`published_copper_mobility`, `published_mobility_a2_per_ps`, `mobility_a2_per_ps`) and refusing NPT campaign boundary (`run_npt_lattice`, `cu_vacancy_comparison`) | Table II record implemented; NPT campaign refuses until `rgpot-core` exports EAM table constructors |
| `error` | Shared `FluxError` enum and `From<rgsaddle::SaddleError>` conversion | Implemented |
| `config` | Internal `with_setters!` macro used by public configuration types | Private module, so it has no importable public path; every generated public setter is listed in the inventory below |

| `rgpot-session` | `dep:rgpot-core` | Enables `engine::rgpot_session::RgpotSessionEngine`, `RgpotSessionConfig`, and `SessionEngineKind` (`OpenMm`, `NbLib`, `Lammps`) |
| `lammpc` | `dep:rgpot-core`, `dep:capnp` | Enables `engine::lammpc::LammpcEngine`, `LammpcConfig`, and `MASS_VELOCITY_TO_EV` over `liblammpc` (`lammpc_session_*`) |

## Configuration structs and field defaults

Every public configuration struct is `#[non_exhaustive]` and provides chainable `#[must_use]` `with_*` builder methods. Setter methods for `Option<T>` fields accept `impl Into<Option<T>>` so passing a bare `T` sets `Some(T)` and passing `None` clears the option.

### `engine::ThermostatConfig`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `gamma` | `f64` | `1.0` | Langevin friction coefficient \(\gamma \ge 0\) in inverse time units; with white noise, `0.0` selects velocity-Verlet NVE, which canonical samplers reject, while a supported colored-noise model can remain thermostatted at `0.0` |
| `temperature` | `f64` | `1.0` | Absolute temperature \(T \ge 0\) |
| `boltzmann` | `f64` | `1.0` | Boltzmann constant \(k_{\mathrm{B}} > 0\) in the engine's energy-per-temperature unit |
| `noise` | `ColoredNoise` | `ColoredNoise::White` | White-noise Langevin or the smart-sampling GLE; each engine must implement the selected model or return `FluxError::InvalidConfig` |

Method: `ThermostatConfig::thermal_energy(&self) -> Result<f64, FluxError>` validates finiteness and domain bounds and returns \(k_{\mathrm{B}} T\).

### `engine::HyperplaneConstraint`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `normal` | `Array1<f64>` | `vec![1.0]` | Unit Euclidean normal \(\mathbf{n}\) (\(\lvert\lVert\mathbf{n}\rVert_2 - 1\rvert \le \text{UNIT\_NORMAL\_TOL}\)) oriented from reactant to product |
| `offset` | `f64` | `0.0` | Scalar offset \(c\) in \(\sigma(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{x} - c = 0\) |

Constructors and methods: `HyperplaneConstraint::new(normal, offset)`, `from_direction(direction, offset)`, `validate(&self)`, and `signed_distance(&self, positions)`.

### `engine::native::NativeConfig`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `masses` | `Array1<f64>` | `vec![1.0]` | Strictly positive per-coordinate masses \(m_i > 0\) (sets `dof = masses.len()`) |
| `thermostat` | `ThermostatConfig` | `ThermostatConfig::default()` | Langevin thermostat parameters |
| `constraint` | `Option<HyperplaneConstraint>` | `None` | Optional active holonomic hyperplane constraint |
| `projection` | `ConstraintProjection` | `ConstraintProjection::Rattle` | Holonomic constraint projection scheme (`Rattle` or `Shake`) |
| `cell` | `Option<[f64; 9]>` | `None` | Optional row-major \(3 \times 3\) periodic simulation box |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Initial deterministic PRNG seed for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck thermal noise |

### `engine::lammpc::LammpcConfig` (feature `lammpc`)

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `atomic_numbers` | `Vec<i32>` | `vec![18, 18]` | Non-empty atomic numbers in live atom order (\(N_{\mathrm{atoms}}\) entries; `dof = 3 * N_atoms`) |
| `type_to_atomic_number` | `Vec<i32>` | `vec![18]` | Non-empty LAMMPS type map (\(\text{type } i+1 \mapsto Z\)) |
| `masses_by_type` | `Vec<f64>` | `vec![39.948]` | Strictly positive per-type masses in amu (length must match `type_to_atomic_number`) |
| `pair_style` | `String` | `"lj/cut 8.5"` | Non-empty LAMMPS `pair_style` specification. Non-ASCII text, NULs, newlines, carriage returns, and semicolons are rejected |
| `pair_coeffs` | `Vec<String>` | `vec!["1 1 0.010323 3.405"]` | LAMMPS `pair_coeff` argument strings. Non-ASCII text, NULs, newlines, carriage returns, and semicolons are rejected |
| `extra_setup` | `Vec<String>` | `vec![]` | Optional setup lines. Empty lines and lines made only of spaces and tabs are omitted. A line of only a newline, carriage return, vertical tab, or form feed is rejected. Every other line must be ASCII. Leading spaces and tabs are kept, and the first word must be `neighbor`, `neigh_modify`, `comm_modify` or `pair_modify`. ASCII controls other than tab, quotes, `$`, `&` and `#` are rejected, as are the words `if`, `partition`, `shell`, `jump`, `python`, `label` and `next`. `include` is rejected except as the `neigh_modify` keyword followed by a group id |
| `boundary` | `String` | `"p p p"` | LAMMPS boundary specification. Non-ASCII text, NULs, newlines, carriage returns, and semicolons are rejected |
| `suffix` | `String` | `""` | Optional LAMMPS accelerator suffix (`omp`, `gpu`, `kk`). Non-ASCII text, NULs, newlines, carriage returns, and semicolons are rejected |
| `thermostat` | `ThermostatConfig` | `ThermostatConfig::default()` | White-noise Langevin thermostat in metal units (\(\gamma\) in \(\mathrm{ps}^{-1}\), \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) in eV); colored-noise models are unsupported and return `FluxError::InvalidConfig` |
| `constraint` | `Option<HyperplaneConstraint>` | `None` | Optional holonomic hyperplane constraint |
| `cell` | `Option<[f64; 9]>` | `Some(diag(30.0, 30.0, 30.0))` | Optional row-major \(3 \times 3\) simulation cell in Å |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Initial deterministic PRNG seed passed to `lammpc_session_md_initialize` |

| `time_step` | `f64` | `0.005` | Integration timestep \(\Delta t > 0\) |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Deterministic PRNG seed |
| `stats` | `StatsConfig` | `StatsConfig::default()` | Batch-means controls for \(\langle \lambda \rangle\) |

### `ohtst::OhtstConfig`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `max_outer_steps` | `usize` | `32` | Maximum bracketing / outer steps (\(\ge 1\)); each reactant relaxation runs at most \(8 \times \text{max\_outer\_steps}\) `rgmin::Lbfgs` iterations, and the reactant search makes at most \(8 \times \text{max\_outer\_steps}\) relaxations |
| `patience` | `usize` | `3` | Consecutive accepted planes within gradient noise (reserved for variational normal optimization) |
| `max_translation` | `f64` | `0.25` | Step size for dividing-surface bracketing, upper cap on curvature probe distance \(\delta\), and per-atom displacement cap of the reactant L-BFGS step (\(> 0\)) |
| `max_rotation` | `f64` | `0.25` | Trust-region cap on normal rotation angle in radians (\(\ge 0\)) |
| `min_overlap` | `f64` | `0.03` | Minimum two-state BAR overlap before warning (reserved for variational normal optimization) |
| `use_mbar` | `bool` | `true` | Combine reversible work across plane nodes with MBAR (reserved for variational normal optimization) |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Deterministic PRNG seed forwarded to curvature sampling |
| `stats` | `StatsConfig` | `StatsConfig::default()` | Batch-means settings for the curvature probe sample |
| `burn_in_steps` | `usize` | `256` | Equilibration steps discarded before the curvature probe sample |
| `min_sample_steps` | `usize` | `128` | Lower bound on curvature-sample steps (\(\ge 2\)) |
| `sample_step_factor` | `usize` | `64` | Multiplier on `max_outer_steps` for curvature-sample length (\(\max(\text{max\_outer\_steps} \times \text{sample\_step\_factor}, \text{min\_sample\_steps})\)) |
| `retention_stride` | `usize` | `16` | Steps between retained configurations in the curvature sample (\(\ge 1\)) |
| `time_step` | `f64` | `0.01` | Integration timestep \(\Delta t > 0\) for the curvature sample |
| `reactant_fmax` | `f64` | `1e-6` | Physical force tolerance on the reactant minimum and on the seed-plane normal slope, finite and \(> 0\), in the engine force unit (eV/Å in metal units). The reactant is a minimum once \(\max_i \lvert F_i \rvert\) is at most this value, and the seed plane is kept verbatim when \(\lvert -\mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{F} \rvert\) is at most this value above the minimum. The default is the gradient tolerance of `rgmin::Lbfgs::default()` on the same infinity norm; a non-finite or non-positive value returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` |

A reactant located to `reactant_fmax` lies about \(\varepsilon = \text{reactant\_fmax} / \kappa\) from the exact minimum. The curvature inferred over a probe of length \(\delta\) then moves by a relative \(\varepsilon / \delta\) and the barrier by about \(\kappa \varepsilon^2 / 2\). At the default and \(\kappa = 1\) eV/Å², \(\delta = 0.25\) Å, these are \(4 \times 10^{-6}\) and \(5 \times 10^{-13}\) eV. Neither force criterion uses `stats::SERIES_FLAT_TOL`: forces at a relaxed minimum or saddle carry rounding noise that grows with the atom count, the total energy, and the coordinate magnitude. `SERIES_FLAT_TOL` remains the relative tolerance of the bisection bracket width.

### `ffs::FfsConfig`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `interfaces` | `Vec<f64>` | `vec![-0.5, 0.0, 0.5]` | Strictly increasing order-parameter levels \(\lambda_0 < \lambda_1 < \dots < \lambda_n\) (\(\text{len} \ge 2\)) |
| `points_per_interface` | `usize` | `128` | Crossing configurations \(M_0\) collected at \(\lambda_0\) (\(\ge 2\)) |
| `trials_per_interface` | `usize` | `256` | Trial trajectories \(K\) launched at each stage (\(\ge 1\)) |
| `max_trial_steps` | `usize` | `10_000` | Maximum integration steps per trial before aborting (\(\ge 1\)) |
| `max_flux_steps` | `usize` | `200_000` | Maximum integration steps during initial flux collection (\(\ge 1\)) |
| `burn_in_steps` | `usize` | `0` | Burn-in steps discarded before counting \(\lambda_0\) crossings |
| `time_step` | `f64` | `0.005` | Integration timestep \(\Delta t > 0\) |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Deterministic PRNG seed |
| `stats` | `StatsConfig` | `StatsConfig::default()` | Batch-means controls for the inter-crossing intervals |

### `pafi::PafiConfig`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `planes` | `usize` | `9` | Number of hyperplanes at equal spacing along the spline path (\(\ge 2\)) |
| `burn_in_steps` | `usize` | `500` | Equilibration steps discarded on each hyperplane before sampling (\(\ge 1\)); every plane and round restarts from the anchor |
| `sample_steps` | `usize` | `4_000` | Production steps added per hyperplane and round (\(\ge 2\)) |
| `time_step` | `f64` | `0.002` | Integration timestep \(\Delta t > 0\) in engine time units |
| `target_error` | `Option<f64>` | `None` | Optional target standard error on \(\Delta F\) (finite, \(\ge 0\)); `None` runs one round |
| `max_rounds` | `usize` | `4` | Maximum sampling rounds (\(\ge 1\)); later rounds run only while `target_error` is set and not reached, and missing it is not an error |
| `zero_temperature_tol` | `Option<f64>` | `None` | Dimensionless tolerance for \(\lvert I_T - \Delta E_0\rvert / \max(E_{\mathrm{unit}}, \lvert\Delta E_0\rvert)\), where both energies use engine energy units and \(E_{\mathrm{unit}}\) is one such unit. `None` uses \(2 (\pi^2 / 12) / (\text{planes} - 1)^2\) (\(\approx 0.0257\) at 9 planes). `Some(value)` uses that finite value (\(\ge 0\)) at every plane count, including the 9-plane value; see the scaling note below |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Base of the per-plane seeds `seed + 4099 * plane + 1000003 * round` (wrapping) |
| `stats` | `StatsConfig` | `StatsConfig::default()` | Batch-means settings for the per-plane force series |

Here \(I_T\) is the trapezoid integral of \(dV/ds\) over the plane anchors and \(\Delta E_0\) is the endpoint energy change. The ratio is relative to \(\lvert\Delta E_0\rvert\) at or above one engine energy unit and bounds the absolute discrepancy below that scale.

`None`, the value stored by `PafiConfig::default()`, sets the effective tolerance to \(2 (\pi^2 / 12) / (\text{planes} - 1)^2\). At the default 9 planes that is the \(\approx 0.0257\) in the table, and changing `planes` scales the tolerance with the trapezoid error. `Some(value)` uses `value` at every plane count, including a value equal to the 9-plane tolerance. The scaling follows a quarter-turn circular arc through a harmonic well. A path that turns further can need a larger explicit tolerance.

### `pafi::FreeEnergyProfile`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---+---+---|
| `arc_lengths` | `Vec<f64>` | Plane coordinates \(s_k\): the mass-weighted chord-length parameter of the spline, from 0 at the first image to the total path length at the last, at equal spacing. Not scaled to \([0, 1]\) |
| `free_energy` | `Vec<f64>` | \(F(s_k) - F(s_0)\) by cubic Hermite quadrature of the plane means; the first entry is 0. With two planes the derivative correction cancels and the rule is the trapezoid rule. With three planes it is exact for a quadratic gradient. With four or more planes it is exact for a cubic gradient |
| `standard_error` | `Vec<f64>` | Standard error of `free_energy`: batch-means plane-force error through the Hermite weights, combined by hypot with the absolute Hermite-minus-trapezoid difference on the same nodes; the first entry is 0. The weighted uncertainty norm is scaled to avoid overflow from finite plane errors |
| `barrier` | `f64` | \(\Delta F\), the global maximum of the Hermite interpolant, which can exceed every sampled value |
| `barrier_error` | `f64` | Standard error of `barrier`: the same combination at `s*` |
| `dividing_index` | `usize` | First plane with the highest sampled free energy. The interpolant maximum recorded in `dividing_arc` can lie on a different interval |
| `dividing_arc` | `f64` | Arc length \(s^*\) of the global maximum of the Hermite interpolant |
| `reactant_frequency` | `f64` | Projected reactant frequency \(\omega_0 = ( \mathbf{n}^\top \mathbf{H}^{-1} \mathbf{n} )^{-1/2}\) from the mass-weighted Hessian \(\mathbf{H}\) and the unit mass-weighted path normal \(\mathbf{n}\) at the first image, in inverse engine time. It is a diagnostic and does not enter `normalized_rate`. Positive definiteness of \(\mathbf{H}\) off the zero modes is certified by a dense eigensolver when \(\text{dof} \le 128\) |
| `reactant_hessian_certified` | `bool` | `true` when the full reactant Hessian was certified positive definite off the zero modes by the dense eigensolver; `false` above 128 coordinates, where dense certification is skipped while finite forces and positive projected curvature remain required |
| `reactant_partition` | `Option<f64>` | \(Z_R = \exp(\ln Z_R)\), in units of \(s\). `Some` when its exponential is finite and positive; otherwise `None` on overflow or underflow, never `Some(0.0)` |
| `reactant_log_partition` | `f64` | \(\ln Z_R\) from the doubled-trapezoid integral \(Z_R = 2\int_0^{s_{\mathrm{end}}} \exp(-(F(s) - F(s_0)) / k_{\mathrm{B}}T)\,ds\) in log space, where \(s_{\mathrm{end}} = s_k\) when \(s^* = s_k\) and \(s_{\mathrm{end}} = s_{k+1}\) when \(s^*\) is interior to \([s_k, s_{k+1}]\) |
| `normalized_rate` | `Option<f64>` | \(k = \sqrt{k_{\mathrm{B}}T / 2\pi}\,\exp(-\Delta F / k_{\mathrm{B}}T) / Z_R\) in inverse engine time: a one-dimensional transition-state rate with the doubled-trapezoid reactant partition and no recrossing correction, not a dynamical rate. `Some` when its exponential is finite and positive; otherwise `None` on overflow or underflow, never `Some(0.0)` |
| `normalized_log_rate` | `f64` | \(\ln k = \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(k_{\mathrm{B}}T / 2\pi) - \Delta F / k_{\mathrm{B}}T - \ln Z_R\), including when the linear rate underflows or overflows |
| `normalized_rate_error` | `Option<f64>` | Delta-method standard error `exp(normalized_log_rate + ln(sigma))`, where \(\sigma\) propagates the plane-mean errors through both \(\Delta F / k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) and \(\ln Z_R\) in log space. `Some(0.0)` when \(\sigma = 0\) or the product underflows. `None` when it overflows or is not finite |
| `quadrature_residual` | `f64` | Largest absolute gap, over the sampled planes, between the Hermite integral of \(dV/ds\) and the energy change from the first plane, in engine energy units. The acceptance check remains the trapezoid comparison in `PafiConfig::zero_temperature_tol` |
