### `opes::OpesMultithermalConfig`

Construct with `OpesMultithermalConfig::range(temp_min, temp_max)`, `OpesMultithermalConfig::set_all(temperatures)`, or `Default::default()` and the setters. `validate(&self)` checks every rule below, and `OpesMultithermal::new` calls it.

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `temperature` | `Option<f64>` | `None` | Simulation temperature \(T_0\) (PLUMED `TEMP`), finite and \(> 0\); `None` takes `ThermostatConfig::temperature` |
| `temp_min` | `Option<f64>` | `None` | Lowest target \(T_{\min}\) (`TEMP_MIN`), finite and \(> 0\); `None` uses \(T_0\). One of `temp_min`, `temp_max`, `temp_set_all` must be set |
| `temp_max` | `Option<f64>` | `None` | Highest target \(T_{\max} \ge T_{\min}\) (`TEMP_MAX`), finite and \(> 0\); `None` uses \(T_0\) |
| `temp_steps` | `Option<usize>` | `None` | Ladder count \(\ge 1\) (`TEMP_STEPS`); `None` estimates it from the observations, or uses one temperature when \(T_{\min} = T_{\max}\). More than one step needs \(T_{\min} \ne T_{\max}\) |
| `temp_set_all` | `Option<Vec<f64>>` | `None` | Explicit non-decreasing targets (`TEMP_SET_ALL`), at least two, all finite and \(> 0\); excludes `temp_min`, `temp_max`, and `temp_steps` |
| `spacing` | `TemperatureSpacing` | `TemperatureSpacing::Geometric` | `Geometric` keeps \(T_{k+1}/T_k\) constant; `LinearInverse` spaces \(\beta\) equally (`NO_GEOM_SPACING`) |
| `pace` | `usize` | `500` (`DEFAULT_PACE`) | MD steps between bias updates (`PACE`), \(\ge 1\) |
| `observation_steps` | `usize` | `100` (`DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_STEPS`) | Unbiased `pace` samples before the first bias (`OBSERVATION_STEPS`), \(\ge 1\) |
| `print_stride` | `usize` | `100` (`DEFAULT_PRINT_STRIDE`) | Updates between entries of `OpesTrajectory::delta_f_history` (`PRINT_STRIDE`), \(\ge 1\) |

### `opes::OpesRunConfig`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `steps` | `usize` | `10_000` | MD steps integrated after the starting configuration |
| `time_step` | `f64` | `0.005` | Integration timestep \(\Delta t > 0\), finite |
| `frame_stride` | `usize` | `1` | MD steps between stored frames, \(\ge 1\); the starting configuration is always the first frame |
| `record_positions` | `bool` | `true` | Store frame positions in `OpesTrajectory::positions` |
| `start_step` | `Option<u64>` | `None` | MD step index of the starting configuration. `None` continues from `OpesMultithermal::last_step` of the shared bias, restored by `from_state`, or starts a new bias at 0. A value must equal that last step when the bias has one, otherwise `run_opes_multithermal` returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` before integrating; a bias restored from a PLUMED state, which has no step, needs a value. The start step plus `steps` must not exceed `u64::MAX`, or the run returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` before touching the engine |

## Public output types, functions, and constants

| Item | Signature / Fields | Description |
|---+---+---|
| `engine::UNIT_NORMAL_TOL` | `64.0 * f64::EPSILON` | Unit Euclidean normal tolerance (\(2^{-46}\)) |
| `engine::HYPERPLANE_PROJECTION_TOL` | `16.0 * f64::EPSILON` | Relative holonomic SHAKE residual tolerance (\(2^{-48}\)) |
| `engine::DEFAULT_REJECTION_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `4_096` | Default maximum redraw attempts in `SurfaceVelocityPolicy::RejectRedraw` |
| `engine::lammpc::MASS_VELOCITY_TO_EV` | `0.000_103_642_696_562_621_75` | LAMMPS metal-unit factor `mvv2e` converting \(\mathrm{amu} \cdot (\text{Å/ps})^2\) to eV |
| `engine::draw_maxwell_boltzmann_velocities` | `(masses, kbt, seed) -> Result<Array1<f64>, FluxError>` | Deterministic Box-Muller draw \(v_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, k_{\mathrm{B}}T / m_i)\) |
| `engine::reflect_velocity_in_place` | `(&mut velocities, masses, normal) -> Result<f64, FluxError>` | Kinetic-energy-preserving mass-weighted Householder reflection across `normal` |
| `stats::SERIES_FLAT_TOL` | `64.0 * f64::EPSILON` | Relative flatness tolerance for constant-series detection |
| `stats::VARIANCE_REL_FLOOR` | `SERIES_FLAT_TOL * SERIES_FLAT_TOL` | Relative variance floor (\(2^{-92}\)) |
| `stats::MIN_STATIONARITY_SAMPLES` | `4` | Minimum window length for `check_stationarity` |
| `stats::BatchEstimate` | `mean`, `standard_error`, `variance`, `batch_count`, `batch_size`, `n_samples`, `n_eff`, `tau_int` | Output of `stats::batch_means(samples, config)` |
| `stats::StationarityReport` | `is_stationary`, `z_score`, `max_z_score`, `drift_slope`, `first_mean`, `second_mean` | Output of `stats::check_stationarity(samples, config)` |
| `stats::effective_sample_size` | `(samples) -> Result<f64, FluxError>` | Geyer initial-monotone-sequence effective sample size \(n_{\mathrm{eff}}\) |
| `kappa::DEFAULT_COMMIT_CHECKPOINTS` | `0` | Default checkpoint count; zero disables early commitment |
| `kappa::kramers_transmission_coefficient` | `(gamma, barrier_frequency) -> Result<f64, FluxError>` | Kramers spatial-diffusion factor \(\kappa_{\mathrm{K}} = \sqrt{1 + \alpha^2} - \alpha\) |
| `kappa::bennett_chandler::Side::committed_from_signed_distance` | `(signed_distance) -> Option<Side>` | Classifies \(s < 0\) as `Some(Side::Reactant)`, \(s > 0\) as `Some(Side::Product)`, and \(s = 0\) on the dividing plane as `None` |
| `kappa::bennett_chandler::BennettChandlerEstimate` | `kappa_t`, `plateau`, `standard_error`, `n_eff`, `plateau_window`, `stationarity`, `positive_flux_count` | Output of `estimate_bennett_chandler` and `shoot_bennett_chandler` |
| `hyperplane::HyperplaneSample` | `plane`, `mean_force`, `standard_error`, `configurations` | Output of `hyperplane::sample_hyperplane(engine, plane, config)` |
| `ohtst::OhtstEstimate` | `plane`, `rate`, `standard_error` | Output of `ohtst::optimize_hyperplane(engine, seed_plane, config)` and `ohtst::optimize_hyperplane_from_minimum(engine, seed_plane, reactant, config)` |
| `ohtst::ReactantMinimum` | `positions`, `fmax` (`ReactantMinimum::new(positions, fmax)`) | Relaxed reactant coordinates, one per engine degree of freedom, and the largest absolute force component \(\max_i \lvert F_i \rvert\) measured there (finite, \(\ge 0\)); output of `ohtst::relax_reactant` and input of `ohtst::optimize_hyperplane_from_minimum`. A per-atom force norm may be declared instead, since it bounds every component |
| `ffs::FfsEstimate` | `initial_flux`, `interface_probabilities`, `rate`, `standard_error` | Output of `ffs::forward_flux_rate(engine, order_param, config)` |
| `pafi::FreeEnergyProfile` | `arc_lengths`, `free_energy`, `standard_error`, `barrier`, `barrier_error`, `dividing_index`, `dividing_arc`, `reactant_frequency`, `reactant_hessian_certified`, `reactant_partition`, `reactant_log_partition`, `normalized_rate`, `normalized_log_rate`, `normalized_rate_error`, `quadrature_residual` | Output of `pafi::pafi_profile(engine, path_images, config)` and `pafi::pafi_profile_dyn(engine, path_images, config)`; see the field table in the configuration section |
| `pafi::IntegralEstimate` | `values`, `error` | Cumulative mean-force integral from the first node, with the per-node truncation taken from the integration rule; the first entry of each is 0 |
| `pafi::MeanForceIntegral` | `cumulative(&self, arcs, gradients) -> Result<IntegralEstimate, FluxError>` | Trait for rules that integrate plane mean forces along strictly increasing arc lengths and report their own truncation |
| `pafi::HermiteIntegral` | Unit struct implementing `MeanForceIntegral` | Cubic Hermite integral of the mean force, the quadrature used by the profile, with truncation taken as the absolute difference from the trapezoid rule |
| `pafi::SimpsonIntegral` | Unit struct implementing `MeanForceIntegral` | Composite Simpson integral of the mean force on unequally spaced planes, with truncation taken as the absolute difference from the trapezoid rule |
| `opes::DEFAULT_PACE`, `DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_STEPS`, `DEFAULT_PRINT_STRIDE` | `500`, `100`, `100` | PLUMED-equivalent defaults of `OpesMultithermalConfig`; PLUMED makes `PACE` compulsory, and 500 is its example value |
| `opes::STATE_ENERGY_FIELD` | `"ecv.ene"` | Temperature column name in state files; a PLUMED input restarting from an `rgflux` state labels the expansion `ecv` and the energy `ene` |
| `opes::TemperatureSpacing` | `Geometric`, `LinearInverse` | Ladder spacing for `temp_steps` and automatic ladders |
| `opes::OpesMultithermal` | `new(config, thermostat)`, `from_state(config, thermostat, reader)`, `from_plumed_state(config, thermostat, reader, temperature, boltzmann)`, `bias(energy)`, `update(step, energy)`, `write_state(writer, time)`, `config`, `temperature`, `boltzmann`, `kbt`, `is_initialized`, `temperatures`, `temperature_range`, `delta_f`, `rct`, `counter`, `last_step` | Bias state. `new` reads only \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\) from the thermostat, and its temperature only when `OpesMultithermalConfig::temperature` is `None`; it checks those values and not the unused ones. It returns `FluxError::NonFinite` unless \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T_0\) and \(1/(k_{\mathrm{B}}T_0)\) are finite and positive, as `MultithermalReweighting::new` requires. It also returns `FluxError::NonFinite` when a target temperature is so far from \(T_0\) that \(\beta_k-\beta_0\), or the temperature recovered from it, is not finite, and when the ladder spacing overflows between finite ends. `bias` returns \(V(U)\) and \(dV/dU\), both zero before initialization. `update` mirrors the PLUMED update order and returns `OpesUpdate`; it ignores a repeat of `last_step` and returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` for an earlier step. An update that returns an error, such as a counter overflow, a non-finite bias, or an `rct` or \(\Delta F\) that overflows to a non-finite value (`FluxError::NonFinite`), leaves the state and `last_step` unchanged, so the step can be retried. `delta_f` is \(\Delta F(T_k)\) in energy units, empty before initialization; `temperatures` is empty until an automatic ladder is fixed. `write_state` adds `# rgflux` comment lines with \(T_0\), \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\), \(T_{\min}\), \(T_{\max}\), and `last_step`; `from_state` returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` when \(T_0\), \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\), or the range differ by more than a relative \(64\varepsilon\), or when only some entries are present, and restores `last_step`. Both constructors return `FluxError::InvalidConfig` for a state `counter` of 0 or `u64::MAX`. A PLUMED state has none of these entries, so `from_state` returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` for it; `from_plumed_state` reads it given the \(T_0\) and \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\) it was written at, which must be finite, positive, and within a relative \(64\varepsilon\) of the configuration and thermostat, and restores with `last_step` `None` |
| `opes::BiasEvaluation` | `bias`, `derivative`, `force_scale()` | \(V(U)\), \(dV/dU\), and \(1 + dV/dU\) |
| `opes::OpesUpdate` | `Idle`, `Observed`, `Initialized`, `Updated { record }` | Effect of one `update` call; `record` marks the updates PLUMED prints to `DELTAFS` |
| `opes::SharedOpesMultithermal` | `new(bias)`, `snapshot()`, `with_bias(f)`, `with_bias_mut(f)`, `last_evaluation()` | Mutex-guarded handle shared by the surface and the driver; a poisoned lock returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` |
| `opes::OpesMultithermalSurface` | `new(inner, shared)`, `inner()`, `shared()`, `ForceSurface::energy_and_forces` | Returns \(U + V(U)\) and \((1 + dV/dU)\mathbf{F}\) from the inner surface and records a `SurfaceEvaluation`. A finite \(U\) and \(V(U)\) whose sum, or a scaled force, is not finite returns `FluxError::NonFinite` and records nothing |
| `opes::SurfaceEvaluation` | `positions`, `potential_energy`, `bias`, `force_scale`, `biased_energy` | Last surface evaluation, used to match engine steps with unbiased energies |
| `opes::DeltaFRecord` | `step`, `rct`, `delta_f` | \(\Delta F\) at initialization and every `print_stride` updates, the rows of the PLUMED `DELTAFS` file |
| `opes::OpesTrajectory` | `steps`, `potential_energies`, `biases`, `force_scales`, `positions`, `delta_f_history`, `bias`, `last_step`, `reweighting()`, `weights(target)`, `delta_f()`, `temperatures()` | Output of `run_opes_multithermal`; frame vectors are aligned one to one, and `weights` returns one normalized weight per stored frame |
| `opes::MultithermalReweighting` | `new(potential_energies, biases, boltzmann, temperature, temp_min, temp_max)`, `from_bias(bias, potential_energies, biases)`, `len`, `is_empty`, `temperature_range`, `log_weights(target)`, `weights(target)`, `effective_sample_size(target)`, `average(target, observable, stats)`, `delta_f(target)` | Per-frame weights \(w_t \propto \exp(\beta_0 V_t + (\beta_0 - \beta) U_t)\) at any target in the range (relative slack \(64\varepsilon\)); `weights` returns a `Vec<f64>` summing to one, aligned with the frames. A target outside the range returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig`. `new` returns `FluxError::NonFinite` unless \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) and \(1/(k_{\mathrm{B}}T)\) are finite and positive at \(T_0\), \(T_{\min}\), and \(T_{\max}\), even when \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\) and each temperature are valid on their own. Finite energies and biases can overflow \(\beta_0 V_t + (\beta_0 - \beta) U_t\), so `log_weights`, `weights`, `effective_sample_size`, `average`, and `delta_f` return `FluxError::NonFinite` for a non-finite log weight instead of NaN weights. `average` also returns `FluxError::NonFinite` when the weighted mean, a linearized deviation \(n w_t (A_t - \bar{A})\), or the standard error of finite observables overflows |
| `opes::ReweightedAverage` | `mean`, `standard_error`, `effective_sample_size` | Weighted mean, batch-means error of the linearized ratio estimator, and Kish effective sample size |
| `network::RateEdge` | `from`, `to`, `rate` (`RateEdge::new(from, to, rate)`) | Directed elementary transition edge in `network::build_rate_table` |
| `cu_reference::CAMPAIGN_UNAVAILABLE` | `&'static str` | Refusal sentence returned while `rgpot-core` lacks EAM table constructors |
| `cu_reference::PublishedMobility` | `doi`, `table`, `equation`, `m0_a2_per_ps`, `m0_unit`, `qm_ev`, `qm_unit`, `qm_sigma_ev`, `ln_m0_sigma`, `coordination` | Pure-Cu Table II comparison record from Daw and Chandross (2021) cite:`dawSluggishDiffusion2021` (DOI `10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.043603`, \(M_0 = 190\,\text{Å}^2/\text{ps}\), \(Q_m = 0.67\,\text{eV}\), \(\sigma(Q_m) = 0.013\,\text{eV}\), \(\sigma[\ln M_0] = 0.13\), \(z = 12\)) |
| `cu_reference::NptLatticeRecord` | `temperature_k()`, `lattice_angstrom()` | Cubic NPT lattice constant \(a(T)\) measured by `run_npt_lattice` |
| `cu_reference::MobilityComparison` | `temperature_k`, `lattice_angstrom`, `ours_a2_per_ps`, `reference_a2_per_ps`, `ratio` | Computed mobility \(M = \Gamma a^2 / z\) alongside the Table II Arrhenius column and their ratio |
| `cu_reference::published_copper_mobility` | `() -> Result<PublishedMobility, FluxError>` | Parse and validate the packaged Table II record for pure Cu |
| `cu_reference::published_mobility_a2_per_ps` | `(temperature_k) -> Result<f64, FluxError>` | Evaluate \(M_0 \exp(-Q_m / k_{\mathrm{B}}T)\) in Å²/ps from the packaged Table II record |
| `cu_reference::mobility_a2_per_ps` | `(total_rate_hz, lattice_angstrom, coordination) -> Option<f64>` | Convert a total hop rate \(\Gamma\) (Hz) to \(\Gamma a^2 / z / 10^{12}\) in Å²/ps |
| `cu_reference::run_npt_lattice` | `(temperature_k) -> Result<NptLatticeRecord, FluxError>` | NPT lattice driver; validates \(T > 0\) and refuses with `CAMPAIGN_UNAVAILABLE` until `rgpot-core` exports EAM table constructors |
| `cu_reference::cu_vacancy_comparison` | `(temperature_k, total_rate_hz) -> Result<MobilityComparison, FluxError>` | Compare a computed vacancy hop rate against Table II at the NPT lattice from `run_npt_lattice` |

### Estimator and sampling entry points

| Item | Inputs | Result and reference |
|---+---+---|
| `stats::batch_means` | Sample slice and `StatsConfig` | `BatchEstimate`; equations and runnable example in `howto.org` |
| `stats::effective_sample_size` | Sample slice | Geyer \(n_{\mathrm{eff}}\); equations and runnable example in `howto.org` |
| `stats::check_stationarity` | Sample slice and `StatsConfig` | `StationarityReport`; Geweke equation and runnable example in `howto.org` |
| `hyperplane::sample_hyperplane` | Mutable engine, plane, and `HyperplaneConfig` | `HyperplaneSample`; constrained mean-force guide in `howto.org` |
| `ohtst::optimize_hyperplane` | Mutable engine, seed plane, and `OhtstConfig` | `OhtstEstimate`; a thermostat without canonical sampling returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` before the search; white noise requires `gamma > 0`, while a supported colored-noise thermostat can use `gamma = 0`; harmonic rate guide in `howto.org` |
| `ohtst::relax_reactant` | Mutable engine and `OhtstConfig` | `ReactantMinimum` relaxed by `rgmin::Lbfgs` to `reactant_fmax`; the engine is restored. `FluxError::ReactantNotRelaxed` when the relaxation ends above the tolerance; shared-reactant guide in `howto.org` |
| `ohtst::optimize_hyperplane_from_minimum` | Mutable engine, seed plane, `ReactantMinimum`, and `OhtstConfig` | `OhtstEstimate` from the supplied minimum without relaxing it. `FluxError::ReactantNotRelaxed` when the declared force, checked before the engine is touched, or the force the engine measures there exceeds `reactant_fmax`; `FluxError::InvalidConfig` when the declared force is negative or not finite, or the minimum is not a minimum along the seed normal |
| `ffs::forward_flux_rate` | Mutable engine, order parameter, and `FfsConfig` | `FfsEstimate`; direct FFS guide in `howto.org` |
| `pafi::group_displacement_scan` | Mutable engine, two 0-based atom-index slices, a 3-vector direction, strictly increasing windows of \(s\), rigid-group slices, and `HyperplaneConfig` | `GroupDisplacementProfile`. \(s = \mathbf{n}\cdot(\mathbf{R}_B-\mathbf{R}_A)\) for the mass-weighted centres of mass. The reported mean force is the plane multiplier divided by \(\lVert\nabla s\rVert_2\). Empty groups, overlapping groups, and a direction that splits a rigid group are rejected. The cell is held fixed and supplies the periodic reference |
| `pafi::GroupDisplacementProfile` | `displacements`, `mean_forces`, `standard_errors`, `free_energy`, `free_energy_error` | Output of `pafi::group_displacement_scan`. `free_energy` is the cubic Hermite integral of `mean_forces`, starting at 0 |
| `pafi::pafi_profile` | Mutable engine, path image matrix, and `PafiConfig` | `FreeEnergyProfile`; PAFI guide in `howto.org` |
| `pafi::pafi_profile_dyn` | Mutable `dyn DynamicsEngine`, path image matrix, and `PafiConfig` | Trait-object form of `pafi_profile` with identical estimator and restoration semantics |
| `pafi::HermiteIntegral::cumulative` | Plane arc lengths and plane mean forces of equal length | `IntegralEstimate` from the cubic Hermite rule; errors on mismatched lengths, fewer than 2 planes, non-finite forces, or arc lengths that do not strictly increase |
| `pafi::SimpsonIntegral::cumulative` | Plane arc lengths and plane mean forces of equal length | `IntegralEstimate` from the composite Simpson rule; errors on mismatched lengths, unless the plane count is odd and at least 3, and on non-finite forces or arc lengths that do not strictly increase |
| `kappa::estimate_bennett_chandler` | Recorded `ReactiveTrajectory` slice and `BennettChandlerConfig` | `BennettChandlerEstimate`; reactive-flux equation in `howto.org` |
| `kappa::shoot_reactive_trajectories` | Mutable engine, dividing surface, initial positions, and `ShootingConfig` | Validated trajectory records used by the Bennett-Chandler estimator |
| `kappa::shoot_bennett_chandler` | Mutable engine, dividing surface, initial positions, and `ShootingConfig` | Shoots trajectories and returns `BennettChandlerEstimate`; runnable guide in `howto.org` |
| `kappa::kramers_transmission_coefficient` | Friction \(\gamma\) and barrier frequency \(\omega_b\) | Analytical Kramers factor; equation and comparison in `howto.org` |
| `opes::run_opes_multithermal` | Mutable engine over `OpesMultithermalSurface`, the shared bias, and `OpesRunConfig` | `OpesTrajectory`; `FluxError::InvalidConfig` when the thermostat is not canonical at \(T_0\) or the engine forces bypass the shared surface; guide in `howto.org` |
| `network::build_rate_table` | State count, `RateEdge` slice, and `NetworkConfig` | Typed `FluxError::Unimplemented` migration boundary; master-equation and kMC guide in `howto.org` |

### Engine trait and concrete methods

Every concrete engine implements the same `DynamicsEngine` contract. The
method paths for each implementation are retained in the generated inventory,
while this table defines their shared semantics.

| Method | Contract |
|---+---|
| `dof` | Return the scalar coordinate count |
| `masses` | Borrow one strictly positive mass per coordinate |
| `positions`, `velocities` | Borrow current unwrapped coordinates or Cartesian velocities |
| `set_positions`, `set_velocities` | Validate shape and finiteness, overwrite state, and project onto an active constraint |
| `cell`, `set_cell` | Read, install, or clear the row-major \(3 \times 3\) periodic cell |
| `thermostat`, `set_thermostat` | Read or validate and install `ThermostatConfig` |
| `constraint`, `set_constraint` | Read, install, or clear `HyperplaneConstraint` |
| `energy_and_forces` | Return \(V(\mathbf{x})\) and physical force \(-\nabla V(\mathbf{x})\) |
| `kinetic_energy` | Return \(\tfrac12\sum_i m_i v_i^2\) |
| `step` | Advance by a finite positive timestep and return `StepReport` |
| `reseed` | Replace the engine stochastic stream |
| `shoot_velocities` | Draw Maxwell-Boltzmann velocities from a deterministic seed |
| `reflect_velocity` | Apply the mass-metric Householder reflection and return \(\mathbf{n}\cdot\mathbf{v}\) |
| `apply_dividing_surface` | Enforce positive normal velocity with `SurfaceVelocityPolicy` |

`ForceSurface::energy_and_forces` is the static-surface counterpart. The
blanket `PointSurface` implementation negates the supplied gradient.
`EindirSurface::new` wraps a differentiable objective and `inner` borrows it.
`StepReport::new` constructs the three end-of-step diagnostics.

| Concrete inherent API | Meaning |
|---+---|
| `NativeEngine::new` | Build the pure Rust engine at the projected origin with zero velocity |
| `NativeEngine::surface` | Borrow its `ForceSurface` |
| `NativeEngine::projection` | Read the active `Rattle` or `Shake` algorithm |
| `NativeEngine::reseed_rng`, `NativeEngine::reseed` | Reset its Langevin stream |
| `RgpotSurface::new`, `RgpotSurface::n_atoms` | Build the optional static callback surface and read its atom count |
| `SessionEngineKind::engine_name` | Return `openmm`, `nblib`, or `lammps` |
| `RgpotSessionEngine::new`, `engine_kind`, `rgpot_version_major` | Build and inspect the optional session adapter |
| `LammpcEngine::new` | Build the direct optional `liblammpc` session engine |

### Bennett-Chandler support types

`Side::from_signed_distance` maps a positive signed coordinate to `Product`
and all other values to `Reactant`. `Side::indicator` returns one or zero for
those states. `ReactiveTrajectory::new` validates finite initial normal
velocity and a non-empty side history. Its public fields are
`initial_normal_velocity` and `sides`. The complete `BennettChandlerEstimate`
field set is listed above.

## Error variants (`FluxError`)

| Variant | Payload | Trigger condition |
|---+---+---|
| `EmptyInput` | `&'static str` | Empty sample slice, trajectory list, mass vector, or direction vector |
| `NoPositiveFlux` | unit | No reactive-flux trajectory has `initial_normal_velocity > 0` |
| `NonStationaryPlateau` | `z_score`, `max_z_score`, `drift_slope` | Candidate Bennett-Chandler plateau window exceeds `max_z_score` |
| `Shape` | `expected`, `got`, `context` | Coordinate, velocity, normal, mass, or trajectory length mismatch |
| `NonFinite` | `&'static str` | `NaN` or infinite input, energy, force, log partition exponent, or intermediate value (whereas finite PAFI log-space partitions and rates whose linear `exp` overflows or underflows `f64` succeed with `None` in `reactant_partition` and `normalized_rate`) |
| `InvalidConfig` | `&'static str` | Configuration parameter or physical invariant out of domain |
| `ConstraintViolation` | `residual`, `tolerance` | Relative hyperplane residual after SHAKE projection exceeds `HYPERPLANE_PROJECTION_TOL` |
| `ReactantNotRelaxed` | `fmax`, `tolerance` | An OH-TST reactant minimum has \(\max_i \lvert F_i \rvert\) above `OhtstConfig::reactant_fmax` |
| `SurfaceRejection` | `max_attempts` | `SurfaceVelocityPolicy::RejectRedraw` exhausted `max_attempts` |
| `Surface` | `String` | Potential energy surface callback failure, converted `rgsaddle::SaddleError`, or an I/O failure reading or writing an OPES state |
| `BackendUnavailable` | `&'static str` | Unlinked external MD session call on `RgpotSessionEngine` or unsupported unconstrained Langevin / constrained NVE mode in `LammpcEngine` |
| `Lammpc` | `String` | Error returned by the `lammpc_session_*` C ABI or Cap'n Proto message decoding. After a null session recreate, later fallible methods and force evaluation return a synthetic `Lammpc` error saying the engine is poisoned. Infallible getters `positions`, `velocities`, `masses`, `dof`, `cell`, `thermostat`, `constraint` and `kinetic_energy` return the last accepted state |
| `InvalidLammpcCommand` | `field` | Command text contains a NUL, newline, carriage return, semicolon, or non-ASCII text. On `extra_setup`, `LammpcEngine::new` returns this error for a NUL, a newline, a carriage return, a semicolon, or non-ASCII text before the forbidden-word scan. `shell;touch` and a line that splits `shell` across a newline return `InvalidLammpcCommand`. After that scan finds no forbidden word, the same error is returned for a quote, `$`, `&`, `#`, an ASCII control other than tab, or a first word other than `neighbor`, `neigh_modify`, `comm_modify` or `pair_modify` |
| `ForbiddenLammpcDirective` | `field`, `directive` | An `extra_setup` line that passed the command-text check and then contains `if`, `partition`, `shell`, `jump`, `python`, `label` or `next` as a word returns this error. `include` does too, except as the `neigh_modify` keyword followed by a group id. This scan runs after the command-text check and before the quote, `$`, `&`, `#`, ASCII-control, and first-word checks. Lines that reach it include `shell touch`, `SHELL touch`, `include setup.in`, `if 1 then shell`, `label a`, `shell#touch` and `if 1 then "shell touch X"`. A semicolon or a newline is rejected before this scan, so those lines do not return `ForbiddenLammpcDirective` |
| `Unimplemented` | `&'static str` | Entry point that is not yet implemented (`build_rate_table`) |

## Binding surface

### C ABI

`rgflux` exports no `extern "C"` function and has no C header in this release.
The optional `lammpc` engine consumes, but does not re-export, the following
`liblammpc` C ABI symbols:

| Purpose | Consumed symbols |
|---+---|
| Session lifecycle | `lammpc_session_create_from_config`, `lammpc_session_destroy`, `lammpc_abi_version` |
| Force evaluation | `lammpc_session_calculate_result`, `lammpc_potential_result_size_for_force_input` |
| Constrained dynamics | `lammpc_session_md_initialize`, `lammpc_session_md_step`, `lammpc_session_md_set_velocities`, `lammpc_session_md_state` |
| Unconstrained NVE dynamics | `lammpc_session_nve_set_positions`, `lammpc_session_nve_set_velocities`, `lammpc_session_nve_step`, `lammpc_session_nve_state` |
| Errors and capabilities | `lammpc_last_error`, `lammpc_capabilities_result` |

All declarations are private implementation details in
`src/engine/lammpc.rs`. The public Rust boundary is `LammpcConfig`,
`LammpcEngine`, and the `DynamicsEngine` implementation listed below.
`LammpcEngine` implements only white-noise thermostat configurations:
colored-noise selections return `FluxError::InvalidConfig` rather than being
treated as canonical sampling.

The `rgpot` feature consumes `rgpot_core::potential::PotentialImpl` through
the external `rgpot_force_input_t` and `rgpot_force_out_t` callback contract.
The `rgpot-session` feature targets the external `rgpot_md_session_*` session
contract for creation, state transfer, force evaluation, reseeding, and
Langevin stepping. It accepts only white-noise thermostat configurations;
colored-noise selections return `FluxError::InvalidConfig` before a session
can silently substitute a different noise model. These symbols are not
declared or exported by `rgflux`. Unavailable session calls return
`FluxError::BackendUnavailable`, while direct `liblammpc` failures return
`FluxError::Lammpc`.

### Python

`rgflux` has no Python extension module, Python package, or type stub in this
release. Python callers need a separate downstream wrapper. Consequently
there are no Python names beyond the Rust inventory below.

## Public API documentation coverage

The release audit uses `cargo-public-api` with every feature enabled. It
counts modules, types, variants, fields, constants, functions, trait methods,
inherent methods, builder methods, and public re-export paths. Generated
trait implementations and blanket implementations are omitted because they
do not add an `rgflux` declaration.

Before the first audit, no qualified public item path had an explicit
qualified entry in the Org reference. The gaps were primarily builder methods,
`DynamicsEngine` methods on concrete engines, optional engine methods,
constants, enum variants, and public re-export paths. The generated inventory
below maps every path to this page and states the current count. The
descriptive tables above document semantics, defaults, constraints, outputs,
and errors. The how-to page documents every estimator workflow with runnable
Rust, equations, and literature citations.

The generated block, including its count, is authoritative. Run
`python3 scripts/generate_api_inventory.py` after changing public Rust API;
`python3 ci/check_public_api_docs.py` fails when the block or its count is
stale, and refuses a hand-written count outside the block.

## Explanation

## Engine-agnostic kinetics

Saddle-point searches in `rgsaddle` and local or Riemannian minimizers in `rgmin` query static energy and gradient surfaces cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,goswamiEnhancedClimbingImage2026,goswamiGaussianProcessSaddle2025,goswamiAdaptivePruning2026,goswamiReproducibleOrchestration2026`. Finite-temperature kinetics additionally requires finite-timestep propagation, thermal velocity seeding, dividing-surface velocity boundary rules, deterministic PRNG reseeding, and holonomic hyperplane constraints.

`rgflux::engine::DynamicsEngine` captures that contract in an object-safe trait. Every trajectory sampler in `rgflux` accepts `&mut E` for `E: DynamicsEngine + ?Sized`, supporting both monomorphized generics and `&mut dyn DynamicsEngine` dynamic dispatch without coupling rate estimators to a particular molecular dynamics package cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,eon2901`.

### How each engine backend is wired

1. *In-process BAOAB + RATTLE/SHAKE reference backend (`engine::native::NativeEngine`)*:
   Integrates unconstrained or hyperplane-constrained Langevin dynamics with white noise (\(\gamma > 0\)) or the smart-sampling colored-noise GLE, and velocity-Verlet NVE dynamics when white noise uses \(\gamma = 0\), through the symmetric BAOAB splitting (half velocity kick *B*, half coordinate drift *A*, exact Ornstein-Uhlenbeck thermostat update *O*, half drift *A*, closing half kick *B*) cite:`leimkuhlerRationalConstruction2012,leimkuhlerGeodesicIntegration2016`. The GLE supplies its own drift and remains canonical when \(\gamma = 0\). Static potential energy surfaces enter through `engine::ForceSurface`, which converts gradients \(+\nabla V(\mathbf{x})\) into physical forces \(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{x}) = -\nabla V(\mathbf{x})\):
   - Any `rgsaddle::PointSurface` via a blanket `ForceSurface` implementation (forwarding optional periodic cells through `eval_in_cell`).
   - Any `eindir_core::DifferentiableObjective<f64>` (as used by `rgmin::Oracle`) wrapped in `engine::EindirSurface`.
   - Any `rgpot_core::potential::PotentialImpl` callback wrapped in `engine::rgpot::RgpotSurface` (feature `rgpot`), exchanging zero-copy CPU DLPack tensors (`rgpot_force_input_t` / `rgpot_force_out_t`).
2. *Direct LAMMPS backend (`engine::lammpc::LammpcEngine`, feature `lammpc`)*:
   Links `liblammpc` and drives its persistent `lammpc_session_*` C ABI with `PotentialConfig` and `ForceInput` Cap'n Proto messages from `rgpot-core`. It supports constrained white-noise Langevin (\(\gamma > 0\)) or zero-friction projected velocity-Verlet (\(\gamma = 0\)) dynamics on a `HyperplaneConstraint` via `lammpc_session_md_initialize`, `lammpc_session_md_step`, and `lammpc_session_md_state` (evaluating endpoint potential energy and physical forces via `lammpc_session_calculate_result` to form the mass-weighted multiplier \(\lambda\)), as well as unconstrained velocity-Verlet NVE (\(\gamma = 0\), no constraint) via `lammpc_session_nve_*` with periodic image-flag coordinate unwrapping. Colored-noise selections return `FluxError::InvalidConfig` instead of being silently treated as white noise. Unconstrained Langevin (\(\gamma > 0\), no constraint) returns `FluxError::BackendUnavailable`, and C ABI failures return `FluxError::Lammpc`.
3. *External MD session adapter (`engine::rgpot_session::RgpotSessionEngine`, feature `rgpot-session`)*:
   Targets `rgpot`'s engine-neutral session C ABI (`rgpot_md_session_*` and `rgpot_core::md_session`) across OpenMM (`SessionEngineKind::OpenMm`, `"openmm"`), GROMACS `nblib` (`SessionEngineKind::NbLib`, `"nblib"`), and LAMMPS (`SessionEngineKind::Lammps`, `"lammps"`). State accessors, Maxwell-Boltzmann velocity draws, and mass-weighted Householder dividing-surface reflections operate in-process; on `develop`, `step`, `energy_and_forces`, and `reseed` return `FluxError::BackendUnavailable` until `rgpot_core::md_session` merges onto `rgpot` `develop`.

### Units across engines and estimators

`rgflux` is unit-consistent with the active `DynamicsEngine`:

- Let \([L]\), \([M]\), \([E]\), and \([T]\) denote the engine's length, mass, energy, and time units (satisfying \([E] = [M][L]^2[T]^{-2}\) in consistent dynamical units, or reduced units where \(k_{\mathrm{B}} = 1\)).
- Hyperplane normals \(\mathbf{n}\) are dimensionless Euclidean unit vectors (\(\|\mathbf{n}\|_2 = 1\) within `UNIT_NORMAL_TOL` \(= 64\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\) cite:`highamAccuracyStability2002`); plane offsets \(c\) have unit \([L]\).
- Potential energies \(V(\mathbf{x})\), kinetic energies \(K(\mathbf{v}) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_i m_i v_i^2\), and thermal energy \(k_{\mathrm{B}} T\) (`ThermostatConfig::thermal_energy`) have unit \([E]\).
- Physical forces \(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{x}) = -\nabla V(\mathbf{x})\) and the holonomic constraint Lagrange multiplier \(\lambda = dA/dc\) have unit \([E][L]^{-1}\).
- First-order transition rates (\(k_{\mathrm{OHTST}}\) in `ohtst`, \(k_{AB}\) in `ffs`, and `normalized_rate` in `pafi`) have inverse time units \([T]^{-1}\).
- Across the `lammpc`, `rgpot`, and `rgpot-session` boundaries, quantities follow LAMMPS `metal` / `rgpot` units: coordinates and box vectors in Å, velocities in Å/ps, forces in eV/Å, energies and \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) in eV, masses in amu (with dynamical conversion factor `MASS_VELOCITY_TO_EV` \(= 1.0364269656262175 \times 10^{-4}\;\mathrm{eV / (amu \cdot \AA^2 / ps^2)}\) in `LammpcEngine`), time steps in ps, and Langevin friction \(\gamma\) in \(\mathrm{ps}^{-1}\).

## Holonomic hyperplane sampling

### Theory

Optimal Hyperplanar Transition State Theory (OH-TST) cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,goswamiAdaptivePruning2026,goswamiEnhancedClimbingImage2026,johannessonOptimizationHyperplanar2001,bligaardOptimizationHyperplanar2005` approximates the dividing surface between reactant and product basins by a hyperplane

\[
\sigma(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{x} - c = 0, \qquad \|\mathbf{n}\|_2 = 1,
\]

with constrained Helmholtz free energy

\[
A(\mathbf{n}, c) = -k_{\mathrm{B}} T \ln \int \delta(\mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{x} - c)\,\exp\!\left(-\frac{V(\mathbf{x})}{k_{\mathrm{B}} T}\right) d\mathbf{x}.
\]

Under diagonal mass matrix \(\mathbf{M} = \mathrm{diag}(m_i)\), the inverse-mass metric norm of \(\nabla \sigma = \mathbf{n}\) is

\[
z = \mathbf{n}^\top \mathbf{M}^{-1} \mathbf{n} = \sum_{i=1}^{D} \frac{n_i^2}{m_i}, \qquad \mu = \frac{1}{z} = \left(\sum_{i=1}^{D} \frac{n_i^2}{m_i}\right)^{-1},
\]

where \(\mu\) is the effective directional flux mass along \(\mathbf{n}\), evaluated via `rgsaddle::flux_mass`. Note that Eq. (24) of Jóhannesson and Jónsson (2001) cite:`johannessonOptimizationHyperplanar2001` writes \(\sum_i m_i n_i^2\), which coincides with \(\mu = (\sum_i n_i^2 / m_i)^{-1}\) only when all coordinates share a common mass. Because \(z\) is independent of position on a flat hyperplane, the Blue Moon geometric Jacobian of Sprik and Ciccotti (1998) cite:`sprikFreeEnergyConstrained1998` is constant across \(\sigma(\mathbf{x}) = 0\), and the thermodynamic mean force equals the canonical average of the holonomic Lagrange multiplier:

\[
\frac{\partial A}{\partial c} = \langle \lambda \rangle_c, \qquad \lambda(\mathbf{x}) = -\frac{\mathbf{n}^\top \mathbf{M}^{-1} \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{x})}{\mathbf{n}^\top \mathbf{M}^{-1} \mathbf{n}} = \frac{\mathbf{n}^\top \mathbf{M}^{-1} \nabla V(\mathbf{x})}{\mathbf{n}^\top \mathbf{M}^{-1} \mathbf{n}}.
\]

`hyperplane::sample_hyperplane` equilibrates the constrained system for `burn_in_steps`, records \(\lambda_t\) over `sample_steps` steps, and estimates \(\langle \lambda \rangle_c\) and its block-averaged standard error \(\sigma_\lambda\) via `stats::batch_means` cite:`flyvbjergErrorEstimates1989,flegalMcmcThirdSignificantFigure2008` while retaining dividing-surface configurations every `retention_stride` steps. The average is a canonical expectation only when the dynamics samples the canonical ensemble, so `sample_hyperplane` requires a supported canonical thermostat. White noise requires \(\gamma > 0\); the smart-sampling GLE remains thermostatted at \(\gamma = 0\) on engines that implement it. NVE dynamics started from the anchor samples an energy shell and returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig`; the mean it gave before this check was biased with no error. In the canonical regime the mean does not depend on \(\gamma\), the constraint scheme (`ConstraintProjection::Rattle` or `Shake`), or the mass distribution, only its standard error and the burn-in it needs do.

### Assumptions and scope

- Positive thermal energy \(k_{\mathrm{B}} T > 0\), a supported canonical thermostat, and strictly positive masses \(m_i > 0\). White noise needs \(\gamma > 0\).

### Engine wiring

`sample_hyperplane` captures an internal `EngineSnapshot` (`positions`, `velocities`, `cell`, `thermostat`, and `constraint`) before modifying the engine and restores those five fields on exit (returning any restoration error if sampling succeeded, or preserving the primary sampling error if both failed). In `NativeEngine` and `LammpcEngine`, two-pass linear SHAKE projects positions to relative residual \(\lvert \mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{x} - c \rvert / (1 + \lvert c \rvert + \|\mathbf{x}\|_2) \le 16\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\) (`HYPERPLANE_PROJECTION_TOL`) cite:`ryckaertShake1977`, and RATTLE projects velocities to the mass-metric tangent space \(\mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0\) cite:`andersenRattle1983,leimkuhlerGeodesicIntegration2016`.

## Optimal hyperplanar transition state theory (`ohtst`)

The dividing surface is a hyperplane with point \(\mathbf{p}\) and unit normal \(\boldsymbol{\nu}\) in mass-weighted coordinates, and its free energy is \(A(\mathbf{p}, \boldsymbol{\nu}) = -k_{\mathrm{B}} T \ln \int \delta(\boldsymbol{\nu} \cdot (\mathbf{q} - \mathbf{p}))\, e^{-V(\mathbf{q}) / k_{\mathrm{B}} T}\, d\mathbf{q}\). The plane that maximizes \(A\) gives the smallest hyperplanar transition state rate cite:`johannessonOptimizationHyperplanar2001`. `ohtst::PlaneOptimizer` climbs \(A\) in both the offset and the orientation, `ohtst::basin_density` gives \(Z_H / Z_R\) on a plane through the minimum, `ohtst::reversible_work` gives \(\Delta A\) from that plane to the optimum, and `ohtst::ohtst_rate` returns \(k = \sqrt{k_{\mathrm{B}} T / 2\pi}\,(Z_H / Z_R)\, e^{-\Delta A / k_{\mathrm{B}} T}\). `ohtst::transmission_coefficient` shoots from the optimal plane for the recrossing factor. Surfaces enter as `rgsaddle::PointSurface`, wrapped in `rgsaddle::MassWeighted` when they are Cartesian.

## Forward Flux Sampling (FFS)

### Theory

Direct Forward Flux Sampling cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,allenSamplingRareSwitching2005,allenSimulatingRareEvents2006,allenForwardFluxEfficiency2006,allenForwardFluxReview2009` computes the rare-event transition rate \(k_{AB}\) from reactant basin \(A\) (\(\lambda(\mathbf{x}) \le \lambda_0\)) to product state \(B\) (\(\lambda(\mathbf{x}) \ge \lambda_n\)) across strictly ordered reaction-coordinate interfaces \(\lambda_0 < \lambda_1 < \dots < \lambda_n\):

\[
k_{AB} = \Phi_{A,0} \prod_{i=0}^{n-1} P(\lambda_{i+1} \mid \lambda_i).
\]

`ffs::forward_flux_rate` evaluates this product in two phases:

1. *Initial escape flux \(\Phi_{A,0}\)*: Starting from an initial state inside basin \(A\) (\(\lambda(\mathbf{x}_0) \le \lambda_0\)), the engine is reseeded from `config.seed`, `burn_in_steps` steps are discarded, and the trajectory is stepped by \(\Delta t = \text{time\_step}\) up to `max_flux_steps` until \(M_0 = \text{points\_per\_interface} \ge 2\) positive-going crossings of \(\lambda_0\) are collected. The crossing detector is armed whenever \(\lambda(\mathbf{x}) \le \lambda_0\) and triggers on the first subsequent step with \(\lambda(\mathbf{x}) > \lambda_0\), storing the phase point \((\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{v})\) and the elapsed waiting time \(\Delta \tau_m > 0\) since the previous crossing (or since burn-in finished). If an excursion reaches the product level \(\lambda(\mathbf{x}) \ge \lambda_n\), the engine is immediately reset to the initial basin-\(A\) phase point \((\mathbf{x}_0, \mathbf{v}_0)\) and re-armed. From the batch-means average waiting interval \(\bar{\tau}\) and standard error \(\sigma_{\bar{\tau}}\) (`stats::batch_means`), the escape flux and its delta-method uncertainty are

   \[
   \Phi_{A,0} = \frac{1}{\bar{\tau}}, \qquad \sigma_{\Phi_{A,0}} = \frac{\sigma_{\bar{\tau}}}{\bar{\tau}^2}.
   \]

2. *Staged conditional probabilities \(P(\lambda_{i+1} \mid \lambda_i)\)*: At each stage \(i = 0, \dots, n - 1\) with \(M_i \ge 2\) stored phase points at \(\lambda_i\), \(K = \text{trials\_per\_interface} \ge 1\) trial trajectories are launched by drawing a starting index \(c \in \{0, \dots, M_i - 1\}\) uniformly, restoring its \((\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{v})\), calling `engine.reseed(seed)` with a fresh deterministic seed from the `StdRng` stream, and stepping up to `max_trial_steps` until \(\lambda(\mathbf{x}) \ge \lambda_{i+1}\) (success; phase point saved for stage \(i + 1\) when \(i + 1 < n - 1\)) or \(\lambda(\mathbf{x}) \le \lambda_0\) (return to basin \(A\), failure). With \(k_c\) trials and \(s_c\) successes launched from starting point \(c\) (\(\sum_c k_c = K\), \(\hat{p}_i = \frac{1}{K}\sum_c s_c\)), the cluster-variance standard error captures heterogeneity across entry points on \(\lambda_i\):

   \[
   \sigma_{p_i} = \frac{1}{K}\sqrt{\frac{M_i}{M_i - 1}\sum_{c=0}^{M_i - 1} (s_c - \hat{p}_i k_c)^2}.
   \]

3. *Composite rate and error propagation*: Combining the initial flux and stage probabilities in quadrature yields

   \[
   \sigma_{k_{AB}} = k_{AB}\sqrt{\left(\frac{\sigma_{\Phi_{A,0}}}{\Phi_{A,0}}\right)^2 + \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \left(\frac{\sigma_{p_i}}{\hat{p}_i}\right)^2}.
   \]

### Assumptions and units

- Does *not* require detailed balance or knowledge of the stationary phase-space distribution, making it applicable to both equilibrium and driven non-equilibrium stochastic systems cite:`allenSimulatingRareEvents2006`.
- Requires stochastic dynamics (e.g. Langevin \(\gamma > 0\)) so that trajectories launched from the same interface phase point \((\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{v})\) diverge after `DynamicsEngine::reseed`.
- Requires strictly increasing interfaces \(\lambda_0 < \lambda_1 < \dots < \lambda_n\) (\(n + 1 \ge 2\)), initial state \(\lambda(\mathbf{x}_0) \le \lambda_0\), at least two collected phase points per interface (\(M_i \ge 2\)), and at least one successful trial per stage (\(\hat{p}_i > 0\)).
- Order parameter \(\lambda(\mathbf{x})\) has any user-chosen unit; \(\Phi_{A,0}\), \(k_{AB}\), and \(\sigma_{k_{AB}}\) have unit \([T]^{-1}\); \(P(\lambda_{i+1} \mid \lambda_i)\) is dimensionless.

### Engine wiring

`forward_flux_rate` drives any `DynamicsEngine` via `positions`, `velocities`, `set_positions`, `set_velocities`, `reseed`, and `step`. On entry it captures an `EngineSnapshot` (`positions`, `velocities`, `cell`, `thermostat`, and `constraint`) and writes all five pieces back before returning (returning any restoration error when the run succeeded, or preserving the run error if both failed). The stochastic stream is left where the flux and trial `reseed` calls placed it.

## Projected Average Force Integration (PAFI)

### Theory

Projected Average Force Integration (PAFI) cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,goswamiEnhancedClimbingImage2026,goswamiReproducibleOrchestration2026,swinburneUnsupervisedCalculation2018` turns a converged minimum-energy path \(\mathbf{X}(s)\), for example a nudged elastic band, into a finite-temperature free-energy profile \(F(s)\) without a global collective variable. The method itself is that of Swinburne and Marinica; the paths it needs come from the band methods cited first.

The path parameter \(s\) is the arc length in the mass-weighted metric, \(ds^2 = d\mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{M}\, d\mathbf{X}\) with \(\mathbf{M} = \mathrm{diag}(m_i)\). At each \(s\) the plane has the unit normal \(\mathbf{n}(s) = \mathbf{M}\mathbf{X}'(s) / \lVert \mathbf{M}\mathbf{X}'(s) \rVert\) and the equation \(\sigma(\mathbf{x}, s) = \mathbf{n}(s) \cdot (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{X}(s)) = 0\), so planes are orthogonal to the path in the metric \(\mathbf{M}\). Neighbouring planes tilt at the rate \(\mathbf{n}' = d\mathbf{n}/ds\), which adds a Jacobian term to the constrained mean force. With \(\lambda\) the Lagrange multiplier of the holonomic constraint on the plane (the same multiplier as in the hyperplane section above):

\[
\frac{dF}{ds}(s) = \Bigl\langle \lambda(\mathbf{x}) \bigl( \mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{X}' - (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{X}) \cdot \mathbf{n}' \bigr) \Bigr\rangle_{\sigma(\mathbf{x}, s) = 0}.
\]

Two limits anchor the estimator:

- *Straight path (\(\mathbf{n}' = \mathbf{0}\))*: the Jacobian term vanishes and \(dF/ds\) is the Sprik-Ciccotti mean constraint force \(\langle \lambda \rangle\) that `hyperplane::sample_hyperplane` samples on a single plane cite:`sprikFreeEnergyConstrained1998`. On the widening double well \(V(x, y) = (1 - x^2)^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}k(x)y^2\) with \(k(x) = 1.5 + 0.5x\), the profile from \(x = -1\) to \(x = 0\) ends at \(\Delta F(T) = \Delta E_0 + \tfrac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T \ln(k(0)/k(-1))\). The integration tests reproduce this value within two standard errors, for unit and anisotropic masses.
- *Zero temperature (\(T \to 0\))*: the sampled points collapse onto the anchor and the integral of \(dF/ds\) becomes the static line integral \(\int \nabla V(\mathbf{X}) \cdot \mathbf{X}'\,ds = \Delta E_0\). `pafi_profile` evaluates that trapezoid sum on the plane anchors before it samples anything and compares it with the end-to-end energy change, see the tolerance note below.

The profile integrates the plane means \(g_k\) with the cubic Hermite rule. On an interval of width \(h\) with endpoint derivatives \(g'\) from a five-point Lagrange window,

\[
\int_{s_k}^{s_{k+1}} g\,ds = \tfrac{h}{2}(g_k + g_{k+1}) + \tfrac{h^2}{12}(g'_k - g'_{k+1}).
\]

With two planes the derivative correction cancels and the rule is the trapezoid rule, exact for a linear gradient. With three planes it is exact for a quadratic gradient. With four or more planes the window carries a cubic gradient exactly. The barrier \(\Delta F\) is the global maximum of that interpolant, searched on every interval, so it can sit between samples and away from the highest sample. The reactant partition function \(Z_R = 2\int_0^{s^*} \exp(-(F(s) - F(s_0)) / k_{\mathrm{B}}T)\,ds\) is evaluated by the doubled-trapezoid rule over the planes up to the dividing segment (through \(s_k\) when \(s^* = s_k\) and through \(s_{k+1}\) when \(s^*\) lies strictly inside \([s_k, s_{k+1}]\)), and the normalized rate is

\[
k = \sqrt{\frac{k_{\mathrm{B}}T}{2\pi}}\,\frac{\exp(-\Delta F / k_{\mathrm{B}}T)}{Z_R}.
\]

The reactant curvature \(\omega_0 = (\mathbf{n}^\top \mathbf{H}^{-1} \mathbf{n})^{-1/2}\) at the first image is reported in `reactant_frequency` for diagnostics and comparison with Vineyard harmonic transition-state theory; it does not enter \(k\). \(\ln Z_R\) and \(\ln k\) are stored in `reactant_log_partition` and `normalized_log_rate`, so a large barrier does not underflow the reported log rate. The linear fields `reactant_partition`, `normalized_rate`, and `normalized_rate_error` are `Option<f64>`. `reactant_partition` and `normalized_rate` are `None` when \(\exp(\cdot)\) of a finite log overflows or underflows `f64`, because a partition or a rate of exactly zero would be read as a true zero (and the partition divides the rate), whereas the log fields keep the value. `normalized_rate_error` is `None` only when the linear error overflows, and is `Some(0.0)` when it underflows, since an absolute error that rounds to zero is negligible next to any representable rate.

What \(k\) is: the transition-state rate of the one-dimensional reduction along the path, with the dividing plane at the maximum of the profile and the reactant partition function \(Z_R\) given by the doubled trapezoid above. It assumes a canonical reactant population, no recrossing (transmission coefficient 1), and a reactant well that the sampled planes between the first image and the dividing plane resolve. For a reactant well that is harmonic along the path normal over the thermal range it approaches Vineyard harmonic transition-state theory, \((\omega_0 / 2\pi)\exp(-\Delta F / k_{\mathrm{B}}T)\), with the transverse entropy already in \(\Delta F\).

What \(k\) is not: it is not a dynamical rate, because recrossing is not estimated, and it is not the Gaussian-reactant rate. On an anharmonic reactant well the doubled trapezoid differs from the Gaussian \(\sqrt{2\pi k_{\mathrm{B}}T} / \omega_0\), and \(k\) follows the integral. \(\Delta F\) is the Hermite integral of the sampled plane means and approaches \(F(s^\ddagger) - F(s_0)\) of the plane foliation as the sampling and the plane spacing are refined.

### What `pafi_profile` does

1. *Spline*: The images become a cubic spline in the chord-length parameter, the sum of \(\sqrt{\sum_j m_j \Delta x_j^2}\) between neighbours. The end second derivatives follow from linear extrapolation of the second derivative, the not-a-knot condition, so the first and last planes keep the curvature of the path. Natural end conditions (zero second derivative) would set \(\mathbf{n}'\) to zero on the end planes and bias the end increments of the profile. Three images give one parabola, two images a straight line. Coincident images are rejected.
2. *Planes*: `planes` planes sit at equal values of the parameter from the first to the last image. Each has an anchor \(\mathbf{X}(s_k)\), the normal \(\mathbf{n}\), and \(\mathbf{n}'\).
3. *Zero-temperature check*: let \(I_T\) be the trapezoid sum of \(dV/ds\) over the anchors and \(\Delta E_0 = V(\mathbf{X}(s_{K-1})) - V(\mathbf{X}(s_0))\). The code compares \(\lvert I_T - \Delta E_0\rvert / \max(E_{\mathrm{unit}}, \lvert\Delta E_0\rvert)\) with the effective `zero_temperature_tol`, where \(E_{\mathrm{unit}}\) is one energy unit of the engine. A mismatch returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` without sampling.
4. *Sampling*: On each plane the engine gets the constraint, is placed at the anchor, receives Maxwell-Boltzmann velocities from the per-plane seed, runs `burn_in_steps` steps, and then `sample_steps` steps that each record \(\lambda\,(\mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{X}' - (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{X}) \cdot \mathbf{n}')\). `stats::batch_means` turns each series into a mean and a standard error.
5. *Integration*: The profile and the dividing plane follow from the Hermite rule on the plane means. At the first image, forces must be finite. The mass-weighted Hessian is checked for positive definiteness off the zero modes by a dense symmetric eigensolver when the coordinate count is at most 128 (\(\text{dof} \le 128\)); above that limit the dense check is skipped and `reactant_hessian_certified` is `false`. At every size, \(\omega_0\) is evaluated from conjugate gradients on central-difference Hessian-vector products of `energy_and_forces`, so non-positive projected curvature is still rejected. The plane errors are independent and propagate in log space through the Hermite weights of the profile and barrier (combined by `hypot` with the Hermite-minus-trapezoid truncation residual) and through the sensitivity of \(\ln k = \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(k_{\mathrm{B}}T / 2\pi) - \Delta F / k_{\mathrm{B}}T - \ln Z_R\) to each plane mean.
6. *Adaptive rounds*: With `target_error` set, steps 4 and 5 repeat for up to `max_rounds` rounds, each adding `sample_steps` samples to every plane, until `barrier_error` is at most the target. The result uses all samples. Missing the target is not an error, so compare `barrier_error` with it.

The seed of plane \(k\) in round \(r\) is `seed + 4099 * k + 1000003 * r` (wrapping), so the planes are independent and a run is reproducible.

### Zero-temperature tolerance

The numerator and denominator in step 3 are energies in the engine's energy units, so their ratio and `zero_temperature_tol` are dimensionless. For \(\lvert\Delta E_0\rvert \ge E_{\mathrm{unit}}\) the check is relative to the endpoint energy change. Below one energy unit it instead bounds the absolute discrepancy to the effective tolerance times one engine energy unit.

`None`, the value stored by `PafiConfig::default()`, makes the effective tolerance \(2 (\pi^2 / 12) / (\text{planes} - 1)^2\), which is \(2 (\pi^2 / 12) / 8^2 \approx 0.0257\) at the default 9 planes. Changing `planes` scales that tolerance. An explicit value passed to `with_zero_temperature_tol` is the tolerance at every plane count, including when it equals the 9-plane value. This scaling follows the trapezoid error on a quarter-turn circular arc through a harmonic well, \(\pi^2 / (12 (\text{planes} - 1)^2)\). A path that turns through more than a quarter circle can need a larger explicit tolerance, which also weakens the guard against inconsistent forces and tangents.

### Assumptions, units, and engine wiring

- Assumes a smooth path of at least two images, with one coordinate per degree of freedom of the engine, whose thermal fluctuations on each plane stay inside the region where neighbouring planes do not intersect, so that \(\mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{X}' - (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{X}) \cdot \mathbf{n}'\) stays positive.
- The plane means are canonical averages, so the engine must run a supported canonical thermostat at positive \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T\). White noise requires \(\gamma > 0\), and `pafi_profile` returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` for its zero-friction NVE mode. A supported colored-noise thermostat can remain canonical at \(\gamma = 0\). In a canonical regime the expected profile does not depend on \(\gamma\); a larger white-noise \(\gamma\) changes the standard error and the burn-in, and a time step too large for \(\gamma\) and the stiffest mode adds an \(O(\Delta t^2)\) bias.
- Every plane starts at its anchor, so a plane whose thermal centre lies far from the anchor needs a long `burn_in_steps`. The first image represents the reactant basin: its forces must be finite, its mass-weighted Hessian off the zero modes must be positive definite when dense certification is performed at \(\text{dof} \le 128\), and its normal curvature must be positive at every size. Above 128 coordinates dense certification is skipped rather than rejected, and the returned `reactant_hessian_certified` diagnostic is `false`.
- Path images, masses and positions use the engine units \([L]\) and \([M]\); the arc length \(s\) is mass-weighted, \([M]^{1/2}[L]\), and equals a length for unit masses. `free_energy`, `standard_error`, `barrier`, `barrier_error`, `target_error`, `quadrature_residual` and \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) are in \([E]\), `time_step` in \([T]\), `reactant_frequency`, `reactant_frequency_error` and `normalized_rate` in \([T]^{-1}\), and `dividing_arc` in the units of \(s\). For Cartesian systems with at least two atoms, the reactant Hessian is probed along each mass-weighted rigid translation and only numerically verified zero modes are projected. Tethered or externally confined translations remain in the curvature, while a path tangent lying entirely in a true translational zero-mode subspace is rejected explicitly. One-dimensional analytic models and single-particle Cartesian confinement are left unprojected.
- `pafi_profile` accepts any `E: DynamicsEngine + ?Sized`, and `pafi_profile_dyn` takes `&mut dyn DynamicsEngine`. The engine must report `StepReport::constraint_force` on constrained steps and implement `energy_and_forces` for the zero-temperature check and for the reactant Hessian.
- Like the other samplers it restores positions, velocities, the periodic cell, the thermostat, and the constraint on return, including on errors. The stochastic stream is left where the last plane reseeded it.
- For adaptive plane placement, `EquidistributionMap` builds the monotone reparametrization \(s \mapsto \sigma(s) \in [0, 1]\) that equidistributes a positive monitor function (\(\lvert dF/ds\rvert\), path normal curvature \(\lVert d\mathbf{n}/ds\rVert_2\), \(\tau_{\mathrm{int}}\)-weighted constraint-force variance, or their normalized combination `MonitorKind::Combined`) with a defensive-mixture floor equal to the path-average monitor \(\bar{w} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L w(s)\,ds\) so planes never collapse cite:`deBoorVariableKnots1973`. `estimate_spectral_tail` fits a Chebyshev / cosine expansion to the mean constraint force and integrated free energy on the current planes to compute a heuristic resolution indicator and flag under-resolved intervals. It is not a rigorous upper bound on interpolation error. `pafi_profile_adaptive` iterates placement, sampling, spectral fitting, and plane insertion until this indicator is at or below the statistical standard error of \(F^*\).
- Adaptive placement is not guaranteed to reduce force calls. In the deterministic regression cases, the localized symmetric double well uses 15 adaptive planes and 670 force calls versus 27 uniform planes and 329 calls at matched barrier error; the asymmetric barrier uses 15 adaptive planes, 670 calls and \(6.45\times10^{-3}\) error versus 10 uniform planes, 125 calls and \(1.01\times10^{-3}\) error. These examples establish placement behavior and tradeoffs, not universal efficiency.
- When replicates are collected on a shared plane grid (such as in the FCC Cu EAM vacancy benchmark cite:`mishinCopperEam2001,sivakCopperDefectDiffusion2021`), `pool_pafi_replicates` pools the per-plane mean constraint forces across replicates before integrating \(F(s)\) and evaluating \(\exp(-F(s^*)/k_{\mathrm{B}}T) / Z_R\), avoiding the positive Jensen bias \(\mathbb{E}[\exp(-F^*/k_{\mathrm{B}}T)] > \exp(-\mathbb{E}[F^*]/k_{\mathrm{B}}T)\) of averaging per-replicate rates. Its delta-method rate error combines the pooled barrier uncertainty and between-replicate reactant-frequency uncertainty in quadrature.

### Displacement between two atom groups

`group_displacement_scan` fixes a different coordinate on a cell that the scan does not change. For atom groups \(A\) and \(B\) with masses \(M_A\) and \(M_B\) and mass-weighted centres \(\mathbf{R}_A\) and \(\mathbf{R}_B\),

\[
s = \mathbf{n}\cdot(\mathbf{R}_B - \mathbf{R}_A),
\]

where \(\mathbf{n}\) is the supplied direction after normalisation. The Cartesian gradient is \((m_i/M_B)\mathbf{n}\) on an atom of \(B\), \(-(m_i/M_A)\mathbf{n}\) on an atom of \(A\), and zero on every other atom. A uniform translation cancels. The existing hyperplane sampler constrains the unit vector \(\boldsymbol{\nu} = \nabla s / \lVert\nabla s\rVert_2\) at offset \(s / \lVert\nabla s\rVert_2\). Its multiplier satisfies \(\langle\lambda\rangle = dF/dc\), and the scan reports

\[
\frac{dF}{ds} = \frac{\langle\lambda\rangle}{\lVert\nabla s\rVert_2}.
\]

The sign is the Sprik-Ciccotti sign: \(\lambda\) is positive when the potential increases with \(s\). The window values of \(dF/ds\) are integrated with the same cubic Hermite rule as the path profile. A periodic cell keeps one reference per window, \(\mathbf{d}_{\mathrm{ref}} = s\mathbf{n}\), and replaces \(\mathbf{R}_B-\mathbf{R}_A\) by \(\mathbf{d}_{\mathrm{ref}}\) plus the minimum image of the residual, using the restricted triclinic unwrapping of the engine cell. Atoms of one rigid constraint group must lie wholly in \(A\), wholly in \(B\), or wholly in neither.

## Reactive-flux recrossing (`kappa` and `kappa::bennett_chandler`)

Transition state theory overcounts the true transition rate whenever trajectories recross the dividing surface before thermalizing. In the Bennett-Chandler reactive-flux formalism cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,goswamiAdaptivePruning2026,bennettMolecularDynamics1977,chandlerStatisticalMechanics1978,andersonStatisticalTheories1973,vanErpNovelPath2003`, trajectories launched from the dividing surface \(\sigma(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{x} - c = 0\) with initial normal velocity \(v_n(0) = \mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{v}(0)\) and post-launch side indicator \(\theta(s(t)) \in \{0, 1\}\) define the time-dependent transmission coefficient

\[
\kappa(t) = \frac{\langle v_n(0)\,\theta(s(t)) \rangle}{\langle v_n(0)\,\theta(v_n(0)) \rangle}.
\]

- `kappa::bennett_chandler::estimate_bennett_chandler` is completely engine-free: it evaluates \(\kappa(t)\) at every step over recorded `ReactiveTrajectory` slices, tests stationarity across the plateau window \([\lfloor f_{\mathrm{start}} T \rfloor, \lceil f_{\mathrm{end}} T \rceil)\) combining temporal batch-means variance with paired trajectory-ensemble early-minus-late shift variance, and computes the plateau standard error from linearized ratio influence values (automatically pairing antithetic \((+\mathbf{v}, -\mathbf{v})\) shots into even batch widths). Values of \(\kappa(t)\) and the plateau are never clamped into \([0, 1]\).
- `kappa::bennett_chandler::shoot_reactive_trajectories` and `shoot_bennett_chandler` clear any active hyperplane constraint on a `DynamicsEngine`, shoot trajectories (including antithetic pairs with independent Langevin noise streams when `ShootingConfig::antithetic` is `true`) from dividing-surface configurations retained by `sample_hyperplane`, restore the engine's constraint, and reduce the ensemble via `estimate_bennett_chandler`. Fixed-length shooting is the default: `KappaConfig::commit_checkpoints = 0` integrates every half to `ShootingConfig::steps` and preserves the full side history. Early commitment is an opt-in optimization. Set a nonzero checkpoint count no greater than `steps` and a strictly positive `KappaConfig::commitment_distance`. Every configuration requires a finite `commitment_distance`. A checkpoint counts toward product commitment only when \(s \ge \text{commitment\_distance}\), toward reactant commitment only when \(s \le -\text{commitment\_distance}\), and otherwise resets the streak. Once the configured number of consecutive checkpoints agrees, that side fills the remaining history. This is safe only when the distance lies inside a physically defined thermalized basin and the window exceeds every relevant recrossing time (for a parabolic Langevin barrier, a conservative scale is several \(1/\lambda_+\), \(\lambda_+ = \sqrt{\gamma^2/4 + \omega_b^2} - \gamma/2\)). A signed-distance threshold is not a proof of irreversible commitment: a trajectory can penetrate deeply and return later, so uncertain systems must retain fixed-length shooting. Steepest-descent endpoint quenching is not yet implemented, so `KappaConfig::quench_force_tol` and `quench_max_steps` remain reserved.
- `kappa::kramers_transmission_coefficient` evaluates Kramers' analytical spatial-diffusion barrier-recrossing factor across a parabolic barrier of unstable frequency \(\omega_b > 0\) under Langevin friction \(\gamma \ge 0\) cite:`kramersBrownianMotion1940`:

  \[
  \kappa_{\mathrm{K}} = \sqrt{1 + \alpha^2} - \alpha = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \alpha^2} + \alpha}, \qquad \alpha = \frac{\gamma}{2 \omega_b}.
  \]

## Correlated time-series diagnostics (`stats`)

Correlated MD and Markov-chain observables underestimate uncertainty when treated as independent draws cite:`goswamiBayesianHierarchical2025,flyvbjergErrorEstimates1989`:

- `stats::effective_sample_size` estimates the integrated autocorrelation time \(\tau_{\mathrm{int}}\) and statistical inefficiency \(g = 2\tau_{\mathrm{int}} \ge 1\) via Geyer's initial positive and monotone sequence estimator cite:`geyerPracticalMcmc1992`, returning \(n_{\mathrm{eff}} = n / g \in [1, n]\).
- `stats::batch_means` partitions a series of length \(n\) into \(a\) non-overlapping batches of width \(b\) (automatically choosing \(\max(\lceil 2\tau_{\mathrm{int}} \rceil, \lfloor \sqrt{n} \rfloor)\) subject to `min_batches` when `batch_size` is `None`) cite:`flegalMcmcThirdSignificantFigure2008`. Series whose spread from the first sample lies within \(\text{SERIES\_FLAT\_TOL}\,(1 + |x_0|)\) return \(x_0\) directly with zero standard error so repeated non-dyadic IEEE-754 floats are never rounded to a neighboring value by summation.
- `stats::check_stationarity` compares the leading `stationarity_first_fraction` (\(0.25\)) and trailing `stationarity_last_fraction` (\(0.50\)) sub-windows via Geweke's two-window \(z\)-score cite:`gewekeEvaluatingAccuracy1992,choderaAutomatedEquilibration2016` alongside the ordinary-least-squares linear drift slope.

## Multithermal OPES (`opes`)

### Theory

On-the-fly probability enhanced sampling with an expanded-ensemble target cite:`invernizziUnifiedApproach2020,invernizziRethinkingMetadynamics2020` builds a bias whose stationary distribution is a uniform mixture of ensembles. In the multithermal case the ensembles are canonical at \(T_1 \le \dots \le T_N\), the run is thermostatted at \(T_0\), and \(\beta = 1 / (k_{\mathrm{B}} T)\). The expansion collective variables are

\[
\Delta u_k(\mathbf{x}) = (\beta_k - \beta_0)\, U(\mathbf{x}),
\]

with \(U\) the potential energy. After \(n\) updates the bias is

\[
V_n(U) = -\frac{1}{\beta_0} \ln \Biggl[ \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k=1}^{N} \exp\bigl(-\Delta u_k + \beta_0 \Delta F_n(k)\bigr) \Biggr],
\]

and the free-energy differences are the reweighted estimates over the samples taken every `pace` steps,

\[
e^{-\beta_0 \Delta F_n(k)} = \frac{\sum_{t \le n} e^{\beta_0 V_t}\, e^{-\Delta u_k(t)}}{\sum_{t \le n} e^{\beta_0 V_t}},
\]

where \(V_t\) is the bias in force when sample \(t\) was taken. At convergence \(\Delta F(k) = -\beta_0^{-1} \ln \bigl( Z(\beta_k) / Z(\beta_0) \bigr)\) with configurational partition functions \(Z\), in energy units as in the PLUMED `DELTAFS` file. Before the first update, \(\Delta F\) is initialized from `observation_steps` unbiased samples by the same expression with \(V_t = 0\), and that initialization counts as one sample in later updates. `rgflux` updates \(\Delta F\) with the incremental log-sum-exp recursion of PLUMED's `OPES_EXPANDED`, including the running constant \(\mathrm{rct} = \beta_0^{-1} \ln \langle e^{\beta_0 V} \rangle\), which matters only for restarts.

The bias depends on the coordinates only through \(U\). With \(\mathbf{F} = -\nabla U\),

\[
-\nabla \bigl(U + V(U)\bigr) = \Bigl(1 + \frac{dV}{dU}\Bigr) \mathbf{F}, \qquad 1 + \frac{dV}{dU} = \sum_{k} w_k \frac{\beta_k}{\beta_0}, \qquad w_k = \frac{e^{-\Delta u_k + \beta_0 \Delta F(k)}}{\sum_j e^{-\Delta u_j + \beta_0 \Delta F(j)}},
\]

so the biased force is the unbiased force scaled by the mixture average of \(\beta_k / \beta_0\), and no collective variable gradient is needed. The factor lies between \(\beta_N / \beta_0\) and \(\beta_1 / \beta_0\). PLUMED applies the same factor in its `ENERGY` action as \(1 - f_U\), where \(f_U = -dV/dU\) is the force on the energy value. `OpesMultithermalSurface` returns \(U + V(U)\) as the engine energy and \((1 + dV/dU)\mathbf{F}\) as the force, so the two are an exact energy and gradient pair.

A frame sampled with bias \(V_t\) reweights to any \(T \in [T_1, T_N]\) with

\[
\ln w_t(T) = \beta_0 V_t + (\beta_0 - \beta) U_t,
\]

which is the sum of the PLUMED `REWEIGHT_BIAS` and `REWEIGHT_TEMP_PRESS` log weights cite:`tribelloPlumed2014,plumedConsortium2019`. `MultithermalReweighting::delta_f` applies the same weights to give \(\Delta F(T)\) at any temperature in the range. The reweighted mean \(\bar{A} = \sum_t w_t A_t\) is a ratio estimator. Its standard error is the batch-means error of \(n w_t (A_t - \bar{A})\), the linearization of that ratio, so the correlation between frames enters through `stats::batch_means`. The Kish effective sample size \((\sum_t w_t)^2 / \sum_t w_t^2\) cite:`kishSurveySampling1965` reports how many independent frames the weights retain at each target.

### Temperature ladders

| `OpesMultithermalConfig` | PLUMED keyword | Ladder |
|---+---+---|
| `temperature` | `TEMP` | Simulation temperature \(T_0\); `None` takes the thermostat temperature |
| `temp_min`, `temp_max` | `TEMP_MIN`, `TEMP_MAX` | Range ends; an unset end is \(T_0\) |
| `temp_steps` | `TEMP_STEPS` | Fixed count. With `TemperatureSpacing::Geometric` the ratio \(T_{k+1} / T_k\) is constant; with `LinearInverse` (`NO_GEOM_SPACING`) \(\beta\) is equally spaced. One step uses the midpoint in \(\beta\) |
| `temp_steps = None` | omitted | Count estimated from the observations: at each end the Kish effective fraction of the observations reweighted by \(e^{-\Delta u}\) halves at a half width in \(\beta - \beta_0\), found by regula falsi to \(10^{-4}\); the count is \(\lceil \lvert \Delta\beta_{\mathrm{range}} \rvert / (\text{left} + \text{right half width}) \rceil\), at least 2. Equal ends, \(T_{\min} = T_{\max}\), skip the estimate and give the single temperature \(T_{\min}\) |
| `temp_set_all` | `TEMP_SET_ALL` | Explicit non-decreasing list of at least two temperatures |
| `pace`, `observation_steps`, `print_stride` | `PACE`, `OBSERVATION_STEPS`, `PRINT_STRIDE` | Update stride (default 500, the PLUMED example value), unbiased samples before the first bias (default 100), and updates between recorded estimates (default 100) |

### Assumptions and engine wiring

- The bias acts on the configurational energy at fixed volume. The engine thermostat must be canonical at \(T_0\): `run_opes_multithermal` returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` when the thermostat \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) differs from the bias \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T_0\), and for white noise with \(\gamma = 0\).
- `run_opes_multithermal` takes any `E: DynamicsEngine + ?Sized` whose forces come from an `OpesMultithermalSurface` sharing the same `SharedOpesMultithermal`, such as `NativeEngine` or an engine over `RgpotSurface`. It checks every step that the shared surface evaluated the engine's current positions and returned the energy the engine reports, and returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` otherwise. Engines that integrate forces outside `rgflux`, such as `LammpcEngine`, cannot take the bias.
- Step indexing follows PLUMED: the starting configuration is MD step `start_step`, the first call to `OpesMultithermal::update` after construction or restart is skipped unless `observation_steps` is 1, and the force at step \(n\) uses the estimates before that step's update. Updates act on absolute multiples of `pace`, so a restart restores the last step from the state and refuses a different `start_step`.
- A state holds \(\Delta F\) and `rct` at one \(T_0\) and \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\). `rgflux` records both and the reweighting range in the state and refuses to restart under different values. PLUMED states lack these entries, and PLUMED itself does not check them, so `rgflux` reads a PLUMED state only through `OpesMultithermal::from_plumed_state`, with the caller stating the \(T_0\) and \(k_{\mathrm{B}}\) it was written at.
- The weights are only as good as the overlap between the sampled energies and each target. Read the Kish effective sample size at each target before trusting an average there. The frames before initialization are unbiased samples at \(T_0\) and reweight correctly, but an early stretch with a rapidly changing bias is usually discarded by reweighting a slice.
- No `rgflux` module consumed reweighting weights before this one. `network::build_rate_table` is still unimplemented, so the per-frame weights are returned as plain `Vec<f64>` for downstream estimators.

## Kinetic rate networks (`network`)

`network` defines `NetworkConfig`, `RateTableConfig`, `RateEdge`, and `build_rate_table` for assembling elementary transition rates \(k_{i \to j}(T)\) cite:`vineyardFrequencyFactors1957,henkelmanLongTimeScale2001` into master-equation graphs and Bortz-Kalos-Lebowitz / Gillespie kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) residence-time tables cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,goswamiConcurrencyAkmc2025,eon2901,bortzNewAlgorithmMonteCarlo1975,gillespieGeneralMethod1976`. `RateEdge::new` validates finite non-negative rate constants, while `build_rate_table` is not yet implemented and returns `FluxError::Unimplemented`.

## Copper vacancy mobility reference (`cu_reference`)

`cu_reference` packages the pure-Cu vacancy mobility column from Table II of Daw and Chandross (2021) cite:`dawSluggishDiffusion2021` (Physical Review Materials 5, 043603, https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevMaterials.5.043603) strictly as a comparison denominator rather than an input to any rate computed by `rgflux`. In Eq. (5) of that paper, the mean-square displacement \(\operatorname{MSD}(t) = \langle\lvert\Delta \mathbf{u}(t)\rvert^2\rangle\) has long-time slope \(6\tilde{M}\) and total vacancy mobility \(M = N_{\mathrm{at}}\tilde{M}\). On an FCC lattice with nearest-neighbour coordination \(z = 12\) and jump distance \(a / \sqrt{2}\), a total vacancy hop rate \(\Gamma\) converts to mobility by \(M = \Gamma a^2 / z\) using the lattice constant \(a(T)\) measured at the simulation temperature.

Table II (p. 043603-8) reports the pure-Cu Arrhenius parameters \(M(T) = M_0 \exp(-Q_m / k_{\mathrm{B}}T)\) (Eq. 3) with \(M_0 = 190\,\text{Å}^2/\text{ps}\) and \(Q_m = 0.67\,\text{eV}\) (matching the FBD static saddle-point energy), together with pure-element statistical sampling errors of \(13\%\) (\(0.13\)) on \(\ln M_0\) and \(0.013\,\text{eV}\) on \(Q_m\). `cu_reference::run_npt_lattice` and `cu_reference::cu_vacancy_comparison` (exercised by `examples/cu_vacancy_adaptive.rs`) refuse explicitly until `rgpot-core` exports `eam_table_from_file` and `eam_table_from_data`, rather than substituting a stored lattice.
